The Unhappiness a city produces is no longer equal to the number of citizens in it, although population still strongly affects Unhappiness. Unhappiness in Vox Populi is caused by several sources, each of them contributing to the total Unhappiness a city has. A detailed overview of the sources of Unhappiness in a city can be seen by hovering over the "[ICON_HAPPINESS_3] Unhappiness" tab in the City Screen. The total amount of Unhappiness in a city cannot exceed the city's population, no matter how much Unhappiness is generated from the different sources. The only exception to this is Unhappiness from Urbanization, which always applies, even if it puts the total Unhappiness of your city above its population. The possible sources of Unhappiness are the following:[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Unhappiness from Needs[ENDCOLOR]: Often, most of the Unhappiness in a city is caused by various Needs. With the exception of Religious Unrest, Unhappiness arises in a city if its output of a certain yield per citizen (like gold per citizen, science per citizen, etc.) is lower than the respective Needs Threshold, a reference value which is calculated based on the yields in other cities worldwide. The lower the city's yield output per citizen is, the higher the generated Unhappiness will be. It is therefore necessary to keep yields in your cities increasing, as your population will become more and more demanding over time due to the stronger competition (other cities grow as well, increasing the Needs Thresholds). Avoiding population growth can help in keeping Unhappiness from Needs manageable, and certain Building and Policies reduce Unhappiness from Needs by a fixed amount. There are five main Needs, four based on different yield types and one based on religious diversity:[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Distress[ENDCOLOR]: Distress is based on the sum of your [ICON_FOOD] food and [ICON_PRODUCTION] production yields. Internal Trade Routes can be used to increase a city's food or production output, and thus counter Distress. The Farming Process also counters Distress.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Poverty[ENDCOLOR]: Poverty is based on the [ICON_GOLD] gold yield of a city. To counteract Poverty, increase the city's gold output, for example by working tiles that provide gold or by constructing buildings like the Market. International Trade Routes give their gold to their city of origin, so sending Trade Routes from impoverished cities can also help counter Poverty. The Wealth process also counters Poverty.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Illiteracy[ENDCOLOR]: Illiteracy is based on the [ICON_RESEARCH] science yield of a city. Constructing science buildings or establishing Trade Routes to more advanced civilizations can help reduce Illiteracy. The Research process also counters Illiteracy.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Boredom[ENDCOLOR]: Boredom is based on the [ICON_CULTURE] culture yield of a city. Boredom is especially concerning, as other civilizations get a tourism bonus toward you if you have high levels of Boredom. Buildings providing culture per turn and Trade Routes to more cultured civilizations can counteract Boredom. Great Works can also be moved to bored cities to increase their culture output. Finally, the Arts process also counters Boredom.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Religious Unrest[ENDCOLOR]: Religious Unrest is produced by religious diversity rather than city yields. If a city has a majority religion, 1 Unhappiness is generated for every 2 citizens not following the majority religion (this base value is affected by Need Modifiers). This can be reduced by using Missionaries, Inquisitors, or Great Prophets to remove religious minorities.[NEWLINE]
[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Other sources of Unhappiness[ENDCOLOR]: In addition to Unhappiness from Needs, there are also some other sources of Unhappiness that can affect a city.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Famine[ENDCOLOR]: If a city's food output is below zero, it gains 1 Unhappiness for each point of food lost per turn. Thus, a starving city can increase Unhappiness tremendously. This often happens when enemy units start pillaging and blocking tiles from being worked, causing mass starvation.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Pillaged Tiles[ENDCOLOR]: A city gains 1 Unhappiness for every two pillaged tiles in its vicinity. People don't like seeing their houses burning and will start generating Unhappiness until you do something about it.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Isolation[ENDCOLOR]: An isolated city produces 1 Unhappiness for every 3 Citizens. A city is isolated if it lacks a City Connection to the capital via a road, Lighthouse, or Trade Route. Note that Isolation can occur if a road or lighthouse connection is broken because of a military blockade. Trade Routes are not directly affected by blockades, but may be pillaged by the enemy units if not protected.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Urbanization[ENDCOLOR]: Each Specialist in the city produces 1 Unhappiness, representing the effects of people living in large cities such as pollution and a high population density. Unlike the other sources of Unhappiness, Unhappiness from Urbanization is always added to the total Unhappiness a city has, even if this puts the total Unhappiness of a city above its population. Some buildings and policies allow a city to have "free" Specialists which generate no Urbanization.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]War Weariness[ENDCOLOR]: If you are in a prolonged conflict or suffer high losses in war, your citizens will be unhappy due to War Weariness. War Weariness develops in every city and can significantly increase the empire's total unhappiness. For more details on War Weariness, see the corresponding entry in the Combat Rules Section.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Public Opinion[ENDCOLOR]: Later in the game, other civilizations might exert Ideological Pressure on you, influencing your citizens. If citizens are less than Content with your choice of ideology, they will generate Unhappiness from Public Opinion. If this Unhappiness is too high and your empire is unhappy, you may be forced to switch Ideologies.

Happiness in your empire can come from the following sources:[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Starting Happiness[ENDCOLOR]: The amount of Happiness that your civilization begins with and the starting Local Happiness in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital are determined by the game's difficulty setting. Starting Happiness will become less important over time as Happiness and Unhappiness from other sources grow.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Natural Wonders and Landmarks[ENDCOLOR]: Discovering Natural Wonders or using Archaeologists to build Landmarks (in your own or in other player's lands) gives you a small Happiness bonus.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]City States[ENDCOLOR]: Mercantile City States provide you with a Happiness bonus if you are friends or allies with them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Vassals[ENDCOLOR]: If you have vassalized other civilizations, they may provide you with some additional Happiness based on their own Approval Rating.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Luxury Resources[ENDCOLOR]: You receive Happiness for each unique Luxury Resource connected to your empire. Luxuries are therefore less vital early on, but also not useless in the late game. Moreover, Monopolies on some Luxury Resources grant additional Happiness to your empire.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Locally Generated Happiness[ENDCOLOR]: Certain Buildings increase your local Happiness in the Cities where they are built. Other sources of Local Happiness include Religious Beliefs, Policies, World Wonders and Events. Note that this does not apply to Puppet Cities and Occupied Cities, which can never generate Local Happiness.

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Corporation Types[ENDCOLOR]: there are seven Corporations available in Vox Populi. Each of these can only be constructed once (and only one per player), so choose wisely! For more on this, see the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Corporations[ENDCOLOR] Tab of the Civilopedia.

The happiness system in Vox Populi is completely revised, favoring neither tall nor wide playstyles. Happiness is now based on a cause-and-effect mechanism that makes your empire feel far more alive, and dynamic, than ever before.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Happiness and Unhappiness are calculated locally for each City in your Empire. When the Local Unhappiness in a City exceeds the Local Happiness, the City grows slower than normally, and Production will be reduced when producing a Settler or Military Unit. This is also indicated by an [ICON_HAPPINESS_3] Unhappiness Icon displayed under the City Banner. Special rules apply for Puppet Cities and Occupied Cities.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The sum of the Happiness in all Cities of your Empire is compared to the sum of the Unhappiness in all of your Cities to determine the Approval Rating, which is displayed on the status line of the Main Screen (in the upper left-hand corner of the game). Watch it carefully. If it starts to drop below 50%, your population is getting restless, resulting in a growth reduction in all cities, a penalty when producing Settlers, and reduced combat strength. If it starts to dip below 35%, you are in trouble. Barbarians will spawn in your empire, and cities may abandon your empire and join other civilizations. You can get an overview of the different sources of your Happiness and Unhappiness by hovering your cursor over the status line.
How many levels of unhappiness can there be?

There are three levels of unhappiness. Unhappy, Unrest, and Revolt. An Unhappy civilization can cause population growth to slow signifigantly, a civilization experiencing Unrest can have many more problems, including combat penalties and open rebellion, and a civilization in Revolt can potentially have cities abandon your empire.
How is Local City Happiness determined?

The Local Happiness of a city is determined as follows:[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Some Happiness is generated locally by the City. This can be through Buildings, Policies, World Wonders or Worked Landmarks.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The total amount of Happiness coming from empire-wide sources (like Luxury Resources or allied City States) is distributed deck-of-cards style among all Cities. This is done automatically, prioritizing Cities that have less Local Happiness than Population. After all cities have Local Happiness equal to their Population, any remainder is distributed deck-of-cards style in order of highest to lowest Population.

The calculation of Unhappiness from Needs is done by comparing a City's yield outputs per population to certain reference values, the Needs Thresholds. These values are based on the global median of yield outputs per population (i.e. the value of yield output per population that is exceeded by exactly 50% of cities worldwide). Only Cities with a population of at least 3 are considered when calculating the median, softening Unhappiness in the very early game. The Needs Thresholds are modified by a number of Needs Modifiers in each City. A positive Need Modifier makes it harder to reach the threshold and might therefore increase local Unhappiness, while a negative one might reduce it. The following modifiers are always applied:[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Capital Status[ENDCOLOR]: The Needs Thresholds of the Capital are increased by 25%.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Empire Size[ENDCOLOR]: Each City in your Empire (excluding the Capital and Puppet Cities) increases the Needs Thresholds in every City by 5%. Additionally, every eight Citizens in your Empire (excluding Citizens in Puppet Cities) increase them by 1%.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Difficulty Level[ENDCOLOR]: On the Difficulty Levels "Settler" and "Chieftain", Needs Thresholds are reduced for human players and increased for the AI. On Difficulty Levels above Chieftain, no modifiers are applied.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Certain Policies and Spy Events can also modify Needs Thresholds in a City. In addition, the Processes that convert Production into some other yield provide a reduction of the respective Need Threshold equal to the conversion rate (which can be increased using Power Plants), e.g. Farming converts 25% of Production into Food and decreases the Distress Need Threshold by 25%.
What causes Unhappiness in Occupied and Resisting Cities?

Cities that are in Resistance or being Razed don't generate any Local Happiness. Instead, they generate Unhappiness equal to the city's population. This can massively decrease the Approval Rating of your empire.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Occupied Cities also don't produce any Happiness. They generate Unhappiness equal to the city's population, to which the regular Unhappiness from Urbanization is added.
What causes Unhappiness in Puppet Cities?

In Puppet Cities, special rules for Happiness and Unhappiness apply. Every 4 citizens in a Puppet City generate 1 Unhappiness. The only other possible source of Unhappiness in a Puppet City is Urbanization, which is calculated the same way as in other cities. In a Puppet City, you cannot control the assigment of specialists and therefore cannot counteract Urbanization unless you annex the city. Puppet Cities don't produce any local Happiness, and they follow their own rules for growth, independent of the Happiness system. The Unhappiness generated by Puppet Cities therefore only makes a difference at the empire level.

When your unhappiness reaches -20, your population will be in "Revolt." At this stage, your empire will experience all the penalties from "Unrest", and your cities may abandon your empire, "flipping" to the civilization that is most culturally influential over your people.
How much happiness does my civilization start with?
The amount of happiness that your civilization begins with is determined by the game's difficulty setting. The moment you construct your first city, that number will begin to decline.
When your happiness is negative and your happiness icon is looking sad, your population is "Unhappy." An unhappy population's growth rate is significantly slowed, as is Production.

When your happiness is negative and your happiness icon is looking angry, your population is experiencing "Unrest." If your population is experiencing Unrest, your cities stop growing altogether, you cannot build any Settlers, and your military units get a nasty combat penalty. Additionally, you might have rebels (barbarians) appear within the borders of your empire.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Remember that unhappiness is not permanent. You can always increase your citizens' happiness - no matter how pissed off they are at you - through the methods outlined above.

Historic Events represent monumental achievements that may occur during a game. These events require planning or user interaction, and are thus a dynamic part of acquiring cultural influence over other civilizations. When one of the following Historic Events is completed, receive a [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism boost with all known Civs based on your recent [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism output:[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Earn a [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great Person[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Build a [ICON_WONDER] World Wonder[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Win a [ICON_WAR] War (Warscore 25+)[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Enter a new [ICON_RESEARCH] Era[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Enter a [ICON_GOLDEN_AGE] Golden Age (Artistry)[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Completing an [ICON_RES_ARTIFACTS] / [ICON_RES_HIDDEN_ARTIFACTS] Archaeological Dig (Artistry)[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] [ICON_CARAVAN] Trade with a Major Civilization (Caravansary, etc)[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] [ICON_CARGO_SHIP] Trade with a Major Civilization (Harbor, etc)[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] [ICON_CARAVAN]/[ICON_CARGO_SHIP] Trade with a [ICON_CITY_STATE] City-State (Policy Only)[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The amount of Tourism received by these events is based on your culture and tourism per turn over the past few turns. The value of this is also adjusted based on the number of cities in your empire and your tourism modifier with the target civ. Finally, the amount of tourism you receive is also modified by a few social policies and ideological tenets, as well as leader traits, buildings, and the number of cities in your empire.

A Barbarian Encampment is a temporary settlement by a group of rampaging barbarians intent upon overthrowing and destroying your civilization. These perpetual thorns in the sides of civilizations are capable of spitting out an unending stream of angry barbarians, all who seek to overrun your cities, pillage your lands and stare lewdly at your women. Encampments near to your cities should be destroyed without question. Encampments nearer to competing civilizations may be left to harass your foes, if you are that kind of sneaky leader...

An Oppidum is a large defended settlement associated with the late La Tene culture. These fortified villages were often built in naturally protected areas and full of circular constructions. In times of conflict, the people who lived in open fields moved to these strategically located compounds to ensure their safety. Oppida could also have other purposes such as control of territory or safeguarding of crops. The most famous oppidum was Alesia, the site of the battle between Julius Caesar and Vercingetorix and the final defeat of the Gauls, ending of Gallic independence in France and Belgium.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE] Oppida can be built by Great Engineers, Merchants, Scientists, and Generals. They cannot be built next to each other. Each oppidum Gives +100% [ICON_STRENGTH] Defense Bonus to units stationed on it. They also improve the yields of adjacent improvements:[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET]+1 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production to Farms[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET]+1 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +1 [ICON_PEACE] Faith to Camps[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET]+1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +1 [ICON_PEACE] Faith to Pastures[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET]+1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold to Mines[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET]+1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +1 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science to Quarries[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET]+1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold and +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture to Plantations[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET]+1 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +1 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science to Lumber Mills[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET]+1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold and +1 [ICON_PEACE] Faith to Fishing Boats

The term "Monolithic Church" (or "rock-hewn church") can be attributed to any church cut from a single stone formation, but is most often used to refer to the complex of 11 churches in Lalibela, Ethiopia. These churches were constructed in the 12th century by King Gebre Mesqel Lalibela, a devout Christian. This 'New Jerusalem' is situated in a mountainous region in the heart of Ethiopia, and is an important center of Christian pilgrimage to this day.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE] Monolithic Churches are found in places besides Lalibela, including many in Tigray. These churches were almost unknown to the outside world until Abba Tewelde Medhin Josief, a Catholic priest, announced the existence of over 120 rock-hewn churches, 90 of which were still in use. Over the next few years, the total of known churches was raised to 153.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE] Monolithic Churches can be built on [ICON_RES_STONE] Stone, and on Hills with no resources and not next to another Monolithic Church.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Provides [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_PEACE] Faith. Instead of Technologies, Monolithic Churches are improved by completing [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Social Policy Branches[ENDCOLOR] and adopting an [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Ideology[ENDCOLOR] or [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Religious Beliefs[ENDCOLOR]:[NEWLINE] +1 [ICON_CULTURE] for every Ancient Policy Branch,[NEWLINE] +1 [ICON_PEACE] for every Medieval Policy Branch,[NEWLINE] +1 [ICON_RESEARCH] for every Industrial Policy Branch,[NEWLINE] +1 [ICON_PEACE] for adopting a Pantheon,[NEWLINE] +1 [ICON_CULTURE] and [ICON_PRODUCTION] for founding a Religion,[NEWLINE] +1 [ICON_CULTURE] and [ICON_PRODUCTION] for enhancing a Religion,[NEWLINE] +1 [ICON_GOLD] for reforming a Religion,[NEWLINE] +2 [ICON_GOLD] for adopting an Ideology.

With increasing awareness of the impact of urbanization upon the environment, there were numerous efforts to try and establish more environmentally friendly and sustainable communities. While these communities always remained somewhat small, particularly compared to the much denser arcologies that began to appear afterwards, they were self-sufficient, and their location in relatively unspoilt areas of the wilderness meant they had a certain appeal for ecotourists.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]This improvement provides +1 [ICON_FOOD] to any Farms or Terraces adjacent.

As military units became increasingly sophisticated, it also became increasingly difficult to help maintain their equipment in the field. The most visible effect of the release of the Pholus Mutagen has been the mutation of plants into fungal growths. The unusual plant forms have been observed to developing neural-like structures that allow them to interpret sensory information from their environments, and even respond with toxins and biochemical attacks against those they consider hostile, making areas overrun by the fungus to be quite hazardous for those unprepared for them to traverse. However, the fungus itself also appears to be living in symbiosis with humans and animals affected by the mutagen, providing them with useful sustenance and other valuable materials such as pharmaceuticals.
This custom improvement provides 5 [ICON_GOLD] Gold and 2 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production to the tile it's built on.

As science has advanced, so have the tools needed to probe deeper into the secrets of the universe. While a lot of research is still conducted on an academic and theoretical level, the tools required to explore the mysteries of quantum mechanics, astrophysics and particle physics require specialized high-tech laboratories and research centres.

The industrial complex is a socioeconomic concept wherein businesses become entwined in social or political systems or institutions, creating or bolstering a profit economy from these systems. Such a complex is said to pursue its own financial interests regardless of, and often at the expense of, the best interests of society and individuals. Businesses within an industrial complex may have been created to advance a social or political goal, but mostly profit when the goal is not reached. The industrial complex may profit financially from maintaining socially detrimental or inefficient systems. Increasingly large and complex collections of factories, assembly plants, foundries, and other such industrial buildings begin to appear, as industries are grouped together to help facilitate production and encourage economies of scale. While the Industrial Site isn't as fully effective as the Manufactory, it can still provide a significant boost to production. The concept was popularized by President Dwight Eisenhower in his Jan. 17, 1961 farewell speech. Eisenhower described a "threat to democratic government" called the military industrial complex. This complex involved the military establishment gaining "unwarranted influence" over the economic, political, and spiritual realms of American society due to the profitability of the US arms industry and the number of citizens employed in various branches of military service, the armaments industry, and other businesses providing goods to the US army. The "complex" arises from the creation of a multilateral economy serving military goals, as well as the paradox that arises from the goal of the multilateralism (sustained profit) as antithetical to the military's theoretical goal (peace).

Scientific advancement has given mankind an increasing number of tools with which to manipulate their environment, but this has also meant that pristine, natural environments have become increasingly scarce. Whether to preserve natural ecosystems, or to encourage an increasing ecotourism industry, more and more Nature Preserves are being set aside.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]This improvement provides 3 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and 2 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science to the tile it's built on.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][ICON_CULTURE]Culture is additionally increased by +1 at campsites, Brazilian firewood lumberyards, polders and Nature Preserve adjacent to the tile.
The Nuclear Vault functions both as a Missile Silo and Fallout Shelter. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Can stash up to 3 Nuclear Missiles and provides Fallout Immunity to units stationed on this tile.

A fallout shelter is an enclosed space specially designated to protect occupants from radioactive debris or fallout resulting from a nuclear explosion. Many such shelters were constructed as civil defense measures during the Cold War. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]During a nuclear explosion, matter vaporized in the resulting fireball is exposed to neutrons from the explosion, absorbs them, and becomes radioactive. When this material condenses in the rain, it forms dust and light sandy materials that resemble ground pumice. The fallout emits alpha and beta particles, as well as gamma rays. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Much of this highly radioactive material falls to Earth, subjecting anything within the line of sight to radiation, becoming a significant hazard. A fallout shelter is designed to allow its occupants to minimize exposure to harmful fallout until radioactivity has decayed to a safer level.

Ancient Ruins are the remains of earlier long-dead civilizations. They are filled with valuable secrets - gold, maps, lost technologies and sometimes even survivors - awaiting discovery by the intrepid explorer. Rich rewards await those who first enter an Ancient Ruin!

Salt Gatherers gather salt from saline lakes. Historically, salt has been valuable as it is not only an essential nutrient but it also adds flavor and can be used to preserve food. Salt is often mined, but it can also be gathered from saline lakes. After it was gathered, use as a preservative was common, and as refrigeration was not available, this was often the only way to keep many food items from deteriorating.

The Kampong can be built by [ICON_WORKER] Embarked Workers on Coastal and Lake Tiles, and not next to another Kampong.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each Kampong yields [ICON_FOOD] Food, [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.

The term ‘Sama-Bajau’ refers to a single ethnic group scattered between the modern day Philippines, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The Sama people live a semi-sedentary life in stilt villages or “kampongs” in coastal shallows, while Bajau refers to nomadic groups living in house boats. The Sama-Bajau defy national and ethnic borders, travelling and fishing between islands on the open ocean. The Sama-Bajau were frequently employed as privateers and raiders by the Srivijayan kingdoms. Bajau-Laut possess unique abilities which allow them to see better underwater, and dive longer and deeper than any other group of humans.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In recent years, the Bajau-Laut have been forced into sedentary lifestyles by various governments, and face discrimination as pagans, outsiders and squatters. A combination of overfishing and modernization threatens the Bajau’s nomadic traditions, as they have been forcibly resettled on land. Still, a few communities of Bajau-Laut ride their lepa lepa across the blue water of Southeast Asia, only traveling to shore a few times each year.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Kampong can be built by [ICON_WORKER] Embarked Workers on Coastal and Lake Tiles, and not next to another Kampong.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each Kampong yields [ICON_FOOD] Food, [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.

A kibbutz is a collective community in Israel that was traditionally based on agriculture. The first kibbutz, Degania, was established in 1909 by predominantly Russian and Eastern European Jewish farmers. Kibbutzim began as an outgrowth of the Bilu movement, a combination of socialism and Zionism set on the agricultural settlement of the Land of Israel in reaction to the Russian Jewish Pogroms.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Today, farming has been partly supplanted by other economies, including industrial plants and high-tech enterprises. In recent decades, some kibbutzim have been privatized and changes have been made in the communal lifestyle. There were 270 kibbutzim in Israel as of 2010; their factories and farms account for 9% of Israel’s industrial, and 40% of its agricultural output, worth over 9.7 billion USD. Some Kibbutzim have developed high-tech and military industries, including military plastics and ammunition.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]May only be built on farms and never adjacent to another Kibbutz. +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production to adjacent Farms and Great Person Tile Improvements.

{TXT_KEY_IMPROVEMENT_MONGOLIA_ORDO_HELP}[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Simply translated, "ordo" means "palace tent." However, an ordo was something much more than just a simple tent - it was the center of the tribe for the nomadic Mongolians.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]An ordo served as the headquarters and main encampment for the Khan and his warriors. Though built for travel, it had style, from simple decorations to carefully sewn patterns. The ordo moved with the Khan and his warriors as they went on campaign, ensuring they always felt at home no matter where they traveled.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]You can construct an Ordo anywhere within your territory, or directly adjacent to your territory. Upon constructing the Ordo, your Military Unit Supply Cap will increase by 1, and your Culture borders will also expand to surround the Ordo on all sides by one hex. If the new Culture border claims hexes already owned by another civilization, you will incur a diplomatic penalty as a result. Unlike the Citadel, any enemy unit which ends its turn next to an Ordo takes no damage.

The Turkish word 'Tersane' is derived from the Venetian 'darsane', from which the English word 'arsenal' is also derived. Though never at the forefront of shipbuilding technology, the Ottomans enjoyed over a century of naval dominance in the Mediterranean following their conquest of Constantinople in 1453. The largest Tersane, constructed at the Golden Horn across from Constantinople, housed over 160 docks, drydocks, storehouses and supply depots, making it one of the largest centers of commerce and industry in the Mediterranean.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE] Ottoman naval power was maintained through its tremendous shipbuilding capacity and its allegiances to the Barbary corsairs of North Africa. This pre-eminence was finally ended at the battle of Lepanto, where a combined Spanish and Venetian armada delivered a crushing defeat to the Ottomans, capturing or destroying more than two thirds of the Ottoman navy. In response, the Ottomans built 250 new vessels within six months.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE] "You come to see how we bear our misfortune. But I would have you know the difference between your loss and ours. In wresting Cyprus from you, we deprived you of an arm; in defeating our fleet, you have only shaved our beard."[NEWLINE] Grand Vizier Mehmed Sokullu, on the defeat at Lepanto, and the capture of Cyprus, which the Ottomans had taken earlier the same year[NEWLINE][NEWLINE] Can be built by Expending a Great Admiral or embarked Great General. Deals 30 damage to adjacent Enemy Units.

A Charbagh is a walled garden divided into four square sections that is distinctive to Indo-Persian culture. These gardens trace their roots to the pairidaeza of the Achaemenid empire, and perhaps back even further to Assyrian garden designs. Charbagh construction was an invaluable a tool of state, demonstrating a king’s ability to bring life to an otherwise desolate area; the angular, ordered construction served as a contrast the chaos of nature. Persian and later Persianized cultures employed garden building as a subtle way to demonstrate the King of King's command over his realm and the natural world within it through the creation of public spaces.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Persian gardens have captured the imaginations of Mediterranean and western thinkers. The pairidaeza is the root of the Greek “paradise”, informing modern notions of an earthly Eden in art and poetry.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Charbagh can be built by [ICON_WORKER] Workers on Land with access to Fresh Water, and not next to another Charbagh.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each Charbagh yields [ICON_FOOD] Food, [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, [ICON_GOLD] Gold, and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. During a [ICON_GOLDEN_AGE] Golden Age, the Charbagh's yields are increased by +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture, in addition to the usual +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]+5% [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People Points in City for each worked Charbagh.

Villae were country homes of upper class roman citizens. Over the progressive conquests and expansion of Roman territories and wealth, the villa evolved from relatively simple getaways for social elites into extravagant centers of sprawling agricultural landholdings called Latifundia, an ancient precursor to today’s agribusinesses. The first latifundia were created from land confiscated from conquered peoples in the early 2nd century BC in Magna Graecia (Southern Italy). The Latifundia system expanded with later conquests into Spain and North Africa. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]These estates depended on forced labor for their productivity, often supplied by the enslavement of the same people who occupied the land before conquest. The Latifundia consolidated agricultural production into larger estates with greater economies of scale; owners re-invested profits by purchasing small neighbouring farms to increase their own holdings. Evicted from their farms and replaced by slave labour, the Roman peasantry were forced to find work in the cities of Rome, though often resorting to squatting and handouts. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Latifundia became the template upon which later European nations would base their imperial experiments. The Spanish are especially noteworthy for patterning the Encomienda system after the late Roman Latifundia. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Cannot be built on Resources or adjacent to a City or another Villa. Cannot be removed once it is built.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]On construction, immediately spawns an Improved [ICON_RES_FIGS] Figs Resource on a tile adjacent to the Villa, and claims that tile if not already owned by Rome.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Provides additional [ICON_CULTURE] Culture on the tile, and +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food in the Capital [NEWLINE]+1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_GOLD] Gold to adjacent Plantations.[NEWLINE]+1 [ICON_FOOD] Food and [ICON_GOLD] Gold to adjacent Farms.

{TXT_KEY_IMPROVEMENT_SIHEYUAN_HELP}[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The stately Siheyuan are a mainstay of Chinese architecture dating back to antiquity. The style is often referred to as a Chinese quadrangle, and is used from relatively dwellings and monasteries to the most grand palaces. The Forbidden City in Beijing is designed as an enormous Siheyuan. All siheyuan are positioned along a east-west axis, with the main entrance facing south. The universality of this plan allows sequential siheyuan to be arranged in long rows, creating sprawling suburbs in many of China's largest cities. The narrow alleyways between these rows of Siheyuan are known as hutongs in northern China, forming long market streets similar to middle-eastern bazaars. Recent changes in city planning and construction have resulted in many historic neighbourhoods being demolished, but there have been coordinated efforts to preserve some districts as a valuable piece of Chinese cultural identity.

{TXT_KEY_IMPROVEMENT_SPAIN_HACIENDA_HELP}[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Haciendas are colonial estates constructed by the Spanish for the administration and extraction of resources from their native subjects. Haciendas were based on grants of property and enterprise, rather than the strict grant of indigenous labor as described by the older Encomienda system. Haciendas were generally large estates, but the nature of the work varied from plantations, to mining, to factories.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The owner of a Hacienda was called a Hacendado, but the wealthy landowners rarely visited their holdings and preferred to live in nearby cities. Day-to-day operations of a Hacienda were the responsibility of hired managers. Some unusually large and profitable Haciendas were the property of the Roman Catholic Church, exacerbating tension between native laborers and their Christian taskmasters.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Hacienda system was abolished in most countries after the dissolution of the Spanish Empire, but with mixed results. Efforts to break apart the large estates into individual holdings for subsistence farmers led to crushing poverty in some South American nations. In contrast, Latin American and Filipino Haciendas were mostly left intact, but without the same legal standing or permissions of their colonial past.

An Isibaya is a Zulu homestead and defensive structure. The Isibaya is laid out in a circular pattern with a cattle enclosure at the centre, ringed by huts, palisades, and mud walls. The layout and function are reminiscent of a European corral, hence the Afrikaans term for Amabaya, "Kraal".[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Cattle were central to the life and economy of the Zulu Kingdom. Cattle were a sign of status, wealth, and power, and were instrumental for feeding and arming the amabutho regiments of the Zulu army.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Isibaya is a unique Zulu Great Person Tile Improvement, replacing the Citadel. It Provides [ICON_CULTURE] Culture, [ICON_RESEARCH] Science, and [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, and gives +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture to adjacent Pastures.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Building an Isibaya places a [ICON_RES_COW] Cattle Resource and claims adjacent tiles.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Units standing on an Isibaya receive +100% [ICON_STRENGTH] Tile Defense. The Jet Fighter is extremely similar in role to its ancestor, the World War II propeller-driven fighter, but there are huge differences in the planes' power, armament, weaponry, computer and communications equipment.[NEWLINE]The best World War II aircraft could fly at best 400 miles per hour, while a modern jet fighter can fly three times that fast. A World War II aircraft could carry one or two machine guns and possibly one or two bombs. A modern fighter can carry a 20mm Gatling gun, 10 or so air-to air missiles, and dozens of different rockets. The vehicle is equipped with sophisticated computers, radar, and communications equipment far exceeding anything available anywhere before in history. Like other aircraft, jet fighters are vulnerable to surface-to air missiles, but their largest threat comes from enemy fighters. Whichever side achieves air superiority will gain a nearly unbeatable advantage in combat.

The tribal Jurchen clans, predecessors to the Manchu Dynasty and its people, inhabited the region known as Manchuria, now in present-day northern China. Before the rise of the Manchu Dynasty in the 17th century, the Jurchen briefly united under the banner of the Jin Dynasty in the 12th century. Throughout their history, the Jurchen were known as skilled hunters and equestrians alike, priding themselves on the talents of their cavalry.

SCENARIO DESCRIPTION[NEWLINE]Blessings be upon you great one -- may the mandate of heaven guide you through these difficult times, for the winds of change are upon us, sweeping over East Asia. The victories of the great Japanese warlord Toyotomi Hideyoshi have at long last unified that island nation. Confident in Japan's new gunpowder weaponry, Hideyoshi now casts his eye to the west. Both the venerable Ming Dynasty in China and their ally the Choson Dynasty in Korea must be vigilant! And there is news of a new power taking shape to the north on the Manchurian Plain. Ready your soldiers, your horsemen, and your navies: all forms of weapons and technology must be brought to bear in the coming struggle for control of the lands surrounding the Yellow Sea![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]VICTORY CONDITIONS[NEWLINE]Japan or the Manchu win by conquering both Seoul and Beijing. China and Korea win by controlling all their original cities any time after the year 1600. If none of these conditions occur, the winner is the civ with the most points when the 100 turns are complete. Note that there are extra points earned for each enemy unit killed and for control of Seoul and Beijing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]SPECIAL RULES[NEWLINE]Buy policies at the start to balance your happiness and gold. The only civ that can build new cities is the Manchu. Korea and China are an allied team that starts the game at war with Japan. Science has been turned off.

This Manchu Unique Unit replaces the standard Knight. It possesses a strong ranged attack, increased movement rate, and earns promotions at a double rate. Unit battles also contribute double the amount of points towards earning a Great General.

Banner Cavalry is a Manchu Unique Unit, available in the Medieval Era. This replacement for the standard Knight moves at an increased rate, earns promotions at a double rate, and contributes twice the amount of points towards earning Great Generals. Banner Cavalry can also attack its enemies from afar, using its powerful ranged attack.

Banner Cavalry is a unique replacement for the Knight, available to the Manchu starting in the Medieval Era. Banner Cavalry possess a strong ranged attack and an increased movement rate (5 points total), allowing it to perform hit and run attacks remarkably effectively. If this wasn't enough, Banner Cavalry also acquires promotions at double the rate of other units, and contributes twice the amount of points towards earning Great Generals. These mounted warriors singlehandedly afford the Manchu control of the open plains.

The Eight Banners, created by Manchu founder Nurhaci in the early 17th century, was a system of administration intended to organize the dynasty's military. Initially created to divide the soldiers into different companies, the banner system later came to utilize ethnically-segregated units, as the Manchu military was made up of Manchu, Han, and Mongol troops who typically didn't intermingle. The Manchu and Mongol banner companies were ideal cavalrymen, their long history of nomadic equestrianism breeding formidable mounted troops.

The Manchu Dynasty of China, also known as the Qing Dynasty, traces its foundations to the Jurchen tribes who inhabited the region historically known as Manchuria. First established in the 17th century by the Jurchen tribal leader Nurhaci, the Manchu under Nurhaci embarked on a campaign of expansion and conquest against the powerful Ming Dynasty. Eventually overthrowing the Ming and laying claim to vast swaths of territory, the Manchu Dynasty ruled China for nearly 300 years, and was the last dynasty of China before the formation of the People's Republic.
The great warlord Toyotomi Hideyoshi has unified Japan. To keep his Samurai busy, his eye now turns west to Korea. Will he be able to expand his empire? Or will Korea's Chinese ally arrive in time?
An additonal Jurchen tribe has heard of the growing Manchu strength and joined the Manchu cause.
Korea has received new guerilla units because of their Righteous Army trait.

The proud and warlike Manchu people greet you. Treat us with respect and you may live to see another sunrise.
Khan of the Later Jin Dynasty

Esteemed chieftain Nurhaci of the Jurchen is credited with uniting the nomadic Jurchen tribes of China and creating the foundations of the Manchu Dynasty. Leading during the latter half of the 16th century, Nurhaci was the first Khan of the Jin Dynasty, which later came to be known as the Qing or Manchu Dynasty following his death. During his reign, Nurhaci set his people on a quest to overtake the rival Ming Dynasty of China and eventually the Choson Dynasty of Korea. Nurhaci is notably credited with the creation of the Eight Banners, an organizational system for his military that divided the troops into banner companies of varying size.
The newly united Manchu tribes have seen how China and Korea have been weakened by the ongoing war with Japan. They take this opportunity to declare war!

Meeting with you is always unpleasant, but I must make sacrifices for the sake of the Siamese people.
Congratulations, you have ruined what was otherwise a pleasant day.
I hope that you might find what you seek here in Siam.
Ah, hello! How shall we celebrate your return to Siam?
The Siamese people are moved by your return to our lands. How may we be of service?
You are victorious, for now. But I shall have my revenge!
Trade is the fruit of a relationship between two great kingdoms. What do you think of this offer, my friend?
Siam wishes to trade. Will you?
A true leader knows that only through cooperation can one achieve enlightenment. Shall we open our borders, and allow free passage between our kingdoms?
Cooperation is the gateway to enlightenment. Come, let us share our lands with each other.
Should you provide us with this gift, I will most undoubtedly spread word of your greatness to all the empires of the world.
A gift to Siam at this time would greatly improve our relationship.
Here are my terms. I urge you to take them.
You would do me great honor by accepting this agreement.
Greetings. I believe that this is fair to both parties. What say you?
I mean no disrespect with this offer, it is simply all that I can scrounge up at the moment.
Your offer is unfair and dishonorable - I expected little else from you. Improve it or be gone.
You must do better than that.
I am sure that you meant me no personal insult, but your offer is unfair to my people. I trust that you will improve it?
Is that the best you can do?
As it stands now, your offer is unfair and would cause me to lose face before my people. Please improve it.
Can you do a little better?
One cannot trade with a person who has no honor. Now leave my sight.
I am sure you meant me no disrespect, but I cannot accept your terms.
I find your offer to be an insult to the Siamese people. I refuse it.
Oh very well. Your terms are acceptable.
We are honored by your suggestion, Friend.
A fair agreement does both parties honor. Agreed.
Be gone, useless wretch! Your very presence brings dishonor to my court!
With great reluctance, I must refuse your request.
I would rather die than submit to such humiliation!
You insolent dog! I will avenge this dishonor!
As a guest and a friend, I can refuse you nothing.
Very well, it appears that I have no choice. But I shall avenge this humiliation; I swear it!
You are playing a dangerous game.
Very well. The next time I shall not be so polite!
Indeed? I trust that you will not live to regret your short-sightedness.
You have been badly defeated, you know. How do you deal with the shame?
What cursed treachery is this? Have you no honor, no shame?
You sad little person. Soon you shall feel the full weight of our mighty science bearing down upon you.
Excellent, excellent! I have been looking for a reason to try out my newly outfitted army, and you have provided me with just the occasion.
The Hall grows weary of your tiresome antics. We shall forcefully liberate your downtrodden, and lead them to enlightenment.
Time waits for no man, and I feel its changeless march growing ever more urgent. You stand in our way, and I have not the resources left for more diplomatic means.
I've experiments to run, research to be done, and here you stand like an aging wall to block my path. I shall remove you.
Where to shall my people look for guidance now? A time of darkness is yet upon us.
My unwavering search for science has blinded me to the true threat to my nation, until it was much too late. Leave me to my darkness.
No, I had so much yet to do…so much yet to discover. You have robbed the world of brilliance in your quest of greed.
You will pay for your multiple crimes and indiscretions, starting now with this.
The Worthies kindly request the aid of your generosity in this, our time of need.
A gift bearing the weight of your station is required to enjoy the benefits of this court.
Welcome to the Joseon Court, friend. I have done much to help my people - can you say the same?
Greetings - I am Sejong of Korea. Have you come seeking wisdom and enlightenment, enjoyed by many in my presence?
Welcome to the fair court of Korea, honored stranger. I am Sejong, enlightened leader of these, my mighty people.
A minor miscalculation. It will not happen again.
How have you done this? What manner of tactics do you employ?
Although the sight of your face fills me with disgust, I shall momentarily persevere for the good of my people.
My friend, we have much to discuss and much to gain from each other.
What better way to work towards friendship than by the sharing of material wealth?
My advisors inform me that our offer is underwhelming. I disagree, but anyways, what do you think?
Trained though you may be in the arts of negotiation, this insulting offer cannot stand as it is. Improve it immediately.
You must do better than that.
I would love to accept your offer as it stands, but I know the Hall wouldn’t approve of my logic.
Is that the best you can do?
While you do much to peak my interest, you’ll need to first yet perfect your asking.
Can you do a little better?
Even an uneducated street urchin would know he was being cheated by this debasing offer. Be gone!
What kind of delusions do you suffer under, to think that such a ploy would work?
Words alone cannot express my sorrow for having to disappoint you.
You presume too much above your station.
While this brings much shame upon me, I do what I must for my nation.
You had but to ask! A wise man shares his bounty amongst his friends, so that all may prosper.
Greed does not become you, leading often to sadness. I hope this is for a more noble cause.
This distasteful behavior is what I expect from Yangpyeong, not you.
It seems more goes on behind that vapid stare than I thought.
What a profound waste of time.
Superior technology, planning, and wisdom triumphs yet again.
You cannot best the Hall of Worthies – my country’s best minds act in concert against you.
As St. George has killed the dragon, so will we rise up and stand against this godless and cruel dragon which has risen to oppress mankind.
It is silence that allows evil to triumph. We will not stand mute and allow you to continue on this mad quest unchecked.
You prey upon the weak around you, ever hungry, never satisfied. After us, who is next? We will stand strong and protect.
We do not elect to return evil for evil, nor indulge in the atrocities which you tend to favor. However, I will not idly sit by and let you do as you please.
We do not come to this decision lightly, but we will fight when necessary. We shall win as we are confident in the victory of good over evil.
I have tried all other avenues, but yet you persist in this madness. I hope, for your sake, your end is swift.
God and history will remember your actions this day. I hope you are ready for your impending judgment.
It saddens me to see that the spirit of the wicked continues to cast its shadow on this world. May you find your own peace, before you lead your people to destruction.
In general, a man who is governed by his conscience will co-operate with his fellow human beings. He knows from whence he comes and where he goes. Do you?
The poor, the sick, the elderly - they require aid. Would even you turn your back on them?
Friend, Ethiopia calls to you in her hour of need. Please do not leave us beaten upon the rocks of providence.
I come humbly seeking your generosity in our time of need. Evil is upon us, and we are not equipped to handle it by ourselves.
A thousand welcomes to our fair nation. I am Haile Selassie, the Ras Tafari Makonnen and Emperor of Ethiopia, your humble servant.
Ethiopia welcomes those who come in peace and friendship. I look forward to a long and bountiful relationship.
Welcome, friend, to my lands of peace and prosperity. I am the Conquering Lion of the Tribe of Judah, the Lord of Lords and King of Kings, but you may call me Haile Selassie.
Misguided people sometimes create misguided ideas, and in turn, misguided actions. It is not too late for you to find the path of truth.
Know that you are being watched by your nation: if you continue to do evil, it will lose hope and confidence in you.

Throughout history, it has been the inaction of those who could have acted; the indifference of those who should have known better; the silence of the voice of justice when it mattered most; that has made it possible for evil to triumph.
It is much easier to show compassions to animals. They are never wicked.
I hope we may yet set aside our differences in the interest of discourse.
Let us dine together and discuss matters of the world. We are not material people at heart, but we have some things that may interest you.
I request that you consider this offer between our two peoples. I believe it will do us both good.
My great wisdom demands that I tell you that your offer is better than ours. Do you like our offer in spite of this knowledge?
What cruelty and ill will do you wish to impart upon my people? I have rarely seen such maliciousness.
You must do better than that.
My friend, I am sure you mean well, but this cannot do. We may be simple people, but we will not be taken advantage of.
Is that the best you can do?
Your offer is very interesting, but it is not quite acceptable. Please rethink this.
Can you do a little better?
This absurdity is an affront to the Lord and his peoples. Be gone, and leave me in peace.
What would you take from me that you have not already? You would turn the land to dust and ash.
A thousand apologies, but we cannot hope to part with this at this time. Is there anything else we may help you with?
I am sorry, but we are bound in our own affairs at the moment. You shall be in our thoughts, however.
I have not the physical means to stop you in this. That may not, however, always be the case.
Any aid in the fight against the wicked and the evil is freely given to those who ask.
You had but to ask. However, I would suggest in the future that you ask more politely.
It is a shame to see you behave in such a manner.
Like a small child you are, unable to grasp the bigger picture.
War is not the only means to stop war in kind - I hope you can see this now. Please, return to your lands and think upon what I have said.
Today is the day on which we defeated out enemy. However, we shall only rejoice in our hearts, and in the spirit of heaven.
Your arrogance will only lead you to defeat!
Your treachery will not go unpunished!
A foolish choice! Now you must suffer the consequences.
None will slow our progress, not even you! Prepare for War!
This world isn't big enough for the both of us, and I'm not going anywhere!
Our spears are parched, and I will quench their thirst with your blood!
My warriors have failed, and so have I failed them.
You have bested me, but my people will always remember my will.
Today you are the victor, but perhaps someday you will not be so lucky.
Give us what we want, or you will be the next in line to fall.
You have something I need — perhaps you can help, friend?
Give me what I want - it's in your best interests.
I am Shaka! Ruler of the Zulu Kingdom! Why have you come?
I stand before you as a warrior...can you say the same?
The mighty Zulu Kingdom approaches...choose your words carefully!
We will shift our tactics...this will not be the end!
We will shift our tactics...this will not be the end!
I have no choice but to offer you a trade.
Will you help my kingdom, friend?
A warrior's word is his honor. Because of this, I must admit that we cannot match your trade.
You must do better than that.
My people would rebel if I accepted such an offer...
Is that the best you can do?
You underestimate our needs...you'll have to do better?
Can you do a little better?
Your offer is an insult to my entire kingdom. No.
Even for a friend, I cannot accept.
Your offer is as weak as you are.
It would be an honor to trade with you.
Your offer is fair, I accept.
You risk your life asking me for such a thing!
Even someone as great as I cannot be so generous.
I have no time for your foolish requests.
If we must, then so be it. You will pay for this.
My kingdom welcomes the opportunity to assist a friend.
We will comply, but you may come to regret your greed.
You are playing a dangerous game.
You may live to regret this.
The fact that you still live is a testament to my restraint.
The fact that you still live is a testament to my restraint.
Remarkable: I did not think you had it in you. Very well, let's have at it.
You hopeless idiot. Your greed will be your downfall.
You fool! You have doomed your people to extinction!
You pose a growing threat to my people. I must destroy you.
You have outlived your usefulness. Prepare for war.
By my beard and belly, your doom is upon you! Prepare for war!
This is terrible! I have been defeated! By my beard and belly, how could this have happened?
My armies have been vanquished and all is lost. How is this possible?
Is this real or is it a nightmare? How could you have defeated me?
You may temporarily stave off your destruction by giving us the following.
My friend, can you not spare the following for your close friend and ally?
It would be in your best interest to give us what we want - the spring campaigning season is nearly upon us and my generals await their orders.
By my beard and belly, I am glad to meet you! I am Suleiman, leader of the mighty Ottomans!
The Ottoman nation greets you, Stranger! I am Suleiman!
Greetings, Stranger! I am Suleiman, leader of the Ottomans! Let us feast to celebrate this grand occasion!
I make it a habit to speak only to great leaders, but I shall make an exception for you. Hurry up now.
Your presence here has put me in a foul mood. What do you want?
Welcome to the Ottoman Empire, jewel of civilization.
The Throne of Osman welcomes you.
Ah, welcome back. The Ottoman Empire is always happy to entertain her friends.
The Lawgiver welcomes you to his court. Come, let us discuss the finer points of leadership.
I congratulate you upon your victory and I hope that the peace will last forever.
I will share a portion of my great wealth if you might be inclined to do the same!
The Ottoman Empire thrives on trade. Come, let us make a deal.
The only way to truly know this existence is to see more of it. By opening our borders, we'll push back the horizon and learn more of this world.
The Ottomans wish to venture into your lands. Will you agree to this?
The Ottoman Empire seems to have hit a bit of a rough patch. Might I ask a good friend for help?
The Throne of Osman asks for your help at this time.
I trust that even you can see that this arrangement is to your advantage.
My friend, is this arrangement acceptable to you?
Come - let us negotiate. Is this to your liking?
This is all we can offer you. I would give you my turban as well, but I cannot live without it.
Your offer is unacceptable. Can you not improve it?
You must do better than that.
Come, come! Would you beggar me? Surely you can do better than that!
Is that the best you can do?
You are as greedy as a fish-monger with twelve children! Surely you can do better than that!
Can you do a little better?
I have no time for your nonsense. Go jump in the Bosporous.
My friend, I think you've been out in the sun too long without your turban.
You occasionally do show a hint of sense. Perhaps there's hope for you after all.
By Thunder, there's an idea! Agreed!
Descendent of apes! Do you honestly seek to extort treasure from me? You must be insane!
Is this the way that friends treat each other? By my beard and belly, I think not!
Why not ask for my first-born son, as well? No!
You have the upper hand, for now. But by my beard and belly, it will not always be so!
Of course! My generosity is famous, is it not?
I suppose it is cheaper to pay you off than it would be to destroy you. Very well.
You are playing a dangerous game.
Very well. The next time I shall not be so polite!
Indeed? I trust that you will not live to regret your short-sightedness.
Do not cross us again, I urge you. Next time I will not be so lenient!
Your true colors are shown at last. How dare you think you can do this to me?
Now darling, tantrums are most unbecoming. I shall have to teach you a lesson.
What, did you think you were the only suitor? Many will come to my aid - you are only one.
You have preyed upon my delicate senses. I would wallow in sorrow, but I think I shall find greater pleasure in destroying you.
It is always a shame to destroy a thing of beauty. Happily, you are not one.
You don't return my gifts, and my messengers come back empty handed. I have come for that which is mine, with force.
The winds of change bring a frost which kills the delicate flower. You have destroyed what this nation held most dear.
Like a child playing with toys you are. My people will never love you, nor suffer this indignation gracefully.
When the sun rises again it will weep for what it sees. The lifeblood of this civilization flows within me, and I am no more.
If I must submit myself to your foolishness, I expect it to be made worthwhile.
Darling, where's my gift? You always bring one when you visit.
All of my suitors and courtiers are expected to grace my presence with gifts.
My, isn't this a pleasant surprise - what may I call you, oh mysterious stranger? I am Theodora, beloved of Byzantium.
I am Theodora, mistress of all the world's wonders and beauties. Impress me, stranger, and I may find you a fitting addition to my collection.
Although I have many admirers, you are among the most esteemed of my guests. You may call me Theodora, favored Empress of Byzantium.
You may have won this round, but I wonder if you truly yet understand the game ...
Tsk, life is boring if you always win. Let's see what you do with this small opportunity.
I hope you disagree, so that I may offer this to more worthy individuals.
Perhaps you would like to share in other activities as well.
I have heard that you adept at certain kinds of ... interactions. Show me.
Oh darling, what a wonderful offer! It is a shame that we can only offer you such trinkets in exchange.
Tsk. I find your antics tiresome. Improve your offer or go away.
You must do better than that.
Hmm ... I was too busy listening to your sonorous voice. Try that again.
Is that the best you can do?
I am intrigued by your honeyed words, but I will need to hear more.
Can you do a little better?
No more. I will not suffer your presence any longer.
Thank you, but not this time.
You forget you are no longer in favor. A thousand times no.
Alas, I have nothing of this kind to offer you. Would you take something ... else in return?
My, you think yourself more important than you truly are. I think not.
It galls me that I must agree to this ridiculousness.
My, aren't you the forward one. Perhaps you do deserve to be rewarded.
You amuse me. I see no reason to deny you this.
I like to see a little backbone in a person. It's very encouraging.
I have underestimated you. I find that ... exciting.
Never mind. You will not always be so impervious to my charms.
I'd say that was quite enjoyable, wouldn't you agree? I do ever so much love winning.
I hope you've learned your lesson. I do dislike having to punish you so much.
You have mistaken our love of peace for weakness - you shall pay!
You infamous villain - you shall regret this!
You shall rue this day, you bloodthirsty villain!
You have proven yourself to be an intractable foe to liberty and freedom - prepare for war!
The American people have spoken. Your wanton aggression leaves us no choice: prepare for war!
Your irresponsible behavior has doomed your people - prepare for war!
All is lost, save for honor. I trust you will be merciful in victory.
The day is yours. I hope you will be merciful in your triumph.
You have defeated us - for now. But the United States shall return!
I congratulate you on your victory.
You would be well advised to give us what we want.
Can you spare the following for a friend and ally in need?
We demand the following from you.
The people of the United States of America welcome you. I trust you are a friend to liberty?
On behalf of the citizens of the United States of America, I bid you welcome.
I am honored to meet you. It is my earnest hope that our two people can live side by side in peace and prosperity.
Well? What business might the likes of you have with the United States?
I find it hard to speak freely with tyrants such as yourself.
How may the President of the United States help you?
Welcome back to the United States of America, my friend.
My study is always open to a friend of liberty.
We welcome peace with your great nation. I pray that no future misunderstanding will come between our two peoples.
I hope that through trade the United States and your great empire might become closer.
Trade is the first step on the road to peace, friend.
The United States feels that opening the borders between our two nations would help to further cement our friendship.
America desires to open its borders to you. Will you do the same?
Discipline is the soul of an army. It makes small numbers formidable; procures success to the weak, and esteem to all.
Government is not reason; it is not eloquent; it is force. Like fire, it is a dangerous servant and a fearful master.

If we desire to avoid insult, we must be able to repel it; if we desire to secure peace, one of the most powerful instruments of our rising prosperity, it must be known, that we are at all times ready for War.
The United States would be indebted to you if you were to provide us assistance.
Your help at this time would be invaluable.
We offer this trade. What is your answer?
Greetings. Can the United States interest you in a trade?
Is the following trade of interest to you?
I do not wish to set a precedent for unfair deals with other nations, therefore I admit that our offer is less valuable than yours.
That is not acceptable. You must do better.
You must do better than that.
I fear that I cannot accede to the trade as it now stands. Would you care to improve your offer?
Is that the best you can do?
I do not think that the trade, as it is currently configured, would be in the United States' best interests. Would you care to improve your offer?
Can you do a little better?
Certainly not. We are not fools.
With utmost respect and friendship, I must decline your offer.
I must decline your offer. It is not in our best interest.
Your proposition is acceptable to the United States.
Are you deranged in your senses? We are a free and noble people! We do not truckle to bullies or blackguards!
I cannot give away our treasure so cavalierly, even to friends. I am no tyrant: I must answer to the people of the United States.
Your demand is an insult to our sovereignty, and we reject it out of hand. You clearly underestimate our resolve.
It appears that I have no choice but to accede to your demand. For the moment.
With pleasure. All you had to do was ask.
Very well. It appears that I have no choice but to accede to your demand. But I warn you not to press us too hard.
You are playing a dangerous game.
Very well. The next time, I shall not be so polite!
Indeed? I trust that you will not live to regret your short-sightedness.
I trust that you have learned that the United States are not to be trifled with!
This wanton disregard for lives will not be tolerated.
You call yourself a ruler of men, but all I see is a barbarian clad in finery.
You have proven yourself an unfit ruler, and I can bear the cries of your people no longer. They will be liberated from your tyranny.
You know what you have done, which has led us to this ... unfortunate turn of events.
As much as I hate war, I consider purging your existence a form of community service.
My God, have pity on my soul; my God, have pity on these, my poor people.
Perhaps it is better this way ... now at least I won't witness your destruction of my beloved nation.
Curse you! I had hoped to deliver my people from all foreign yokes, but it seems they shall continue to suffer under yours.
I shall let you continue in your miserable existence, if you appease me.
Your assistance would be greatly appreciated, friend. Your benevolent generosity is renowned.
A small token of your gratitude would be appreciated at this juncture.
I am William of Orange, of the Netherlands. Did you need something? I'm quite busy.
What business do you have in the Netherlands - I am William of Orange, its sovereign ruler.
Welcome to the court of William of Orange, father of the Netherlands. Don't just stand there ... what do you want?
... Inconceivable! What trickery have you used to best me?
I will remember this. Mark my words.
There is one certain means by which I can be sure never to see my country's ruin - I will die in the last ditch.
It is not necessary to hope in order to act, nor to succeed in order to persevere.
My people come before my pride, as bitter as this is.
I believe both our peoples may stand to profit from this arrangement.
Come, I believe I have something which will interest you.
I want what you offer, but I am not sure you will want what I offer. In spite of this, do you accept?
You are beginning to remind me of my second wife, and she was quite mad ...
You must do better than that.
I cannot accept this with a clear conscience, not yet ...
Is that the best you can do?
I still do not understand what about this is supposed to interest me.
Can you do a little better?
I'm beginning to suspect this is some plot to neutralize me. Go away!
For no terms under Heaven will this ever be agreeable.
Not this time, friend. We have our own troubles to deal with.
We are always willing to help an ally in need.
This will be the last time, I promise you.
May this serve as a lesson to you ... hopefully it will be remembered.
You're no better than a sad, foreign mercenary. You'll need to do much better to beat me.
Fool! We shall gut you like a carp!
Barbarian fool! We shall destroy you!
Curse you! You will rue this day for the rest of your brief existence!
You have outlived your usefulness. Die.
You are no longer of any use to us. Die.
You have insulted me for the last time! Die!
You have destroyed me. I congratulate you. If the circumstances had been reversed, I would have happily done the same to you.
I am finished in this world. Perhaps I shall have my revenge in the next.
You have proven yourself a cunning and worthy adversary. I commend you on your victory.
If you wish to continue your miserable existence, then give us the following.
My friend, China has need of your assistance. I am sure we can count on your support.
I encourage you to give us the following, as the alternative is likely to be far more expensive to all involved.
Welcome. I am Wu Zetian, Empress of China. We do not look for conflict with others, but we will respond forcefully to protect our interests.
Greetings. I am the Empress Wu Zetian. China seeks peace to pursue its own development. Leave us alone and we shall do the same for you.
Greetings. I am Wu Zetian, Empress of China. China seeks peaceful coexistence and fair trade, but will respond forcefully to aggression. I hope you are of like mind.
Disrespect the mighty Chinese Empire at your peril, "friend."
I have little patience for upstarts like you.
Welcome. What brings you to rich and powerful China?
The Empress Dowager of China greets you.
Greetings, my friend. We have to look out for each other these days, don't you think?
I am late for my morning ritual, but I can spare a moment for you, if you'd like.
China welcomes peace with all of her neighbors. I trust that there will be no need to repeat this unpleasant business in the future.
China has many rare and valuable goods. Let us make an exchange.
The riches of China are yours to command. For a price.
I believe opening our borders will help culture and arts in both of our empires to flourish.
An open borders agreement will lead to great things.
As much as it pains me to sacrifice China's pride in this manner, I must ask for your assistance.
It pains me to ask, but could you help the Empress Dowager of China?
Here is our offer. You may take it or leave it.
My friend, do you find this offer acceptable?
We believe that fair trade benefits all those involved. What do you think this offer?
The Heavenly Throne is, shamefully, unable to match your glorious offer. We can, however, offer you this.
Do you take us for ignorant peasants? That offer is unacceptable. Improve it.
You must do better than that.
I deeply regret that I cannot accept your offer as it presently stands. Please improve it.
Is that the best you can do?
We cannot accept that. Please improve your offer.
Can you do a little better?
Your arrogance is matched only by your ignorance. We decline your contemptible offer.
I fear that we cannot accept your offer at this time.
Certainly. I congratulate you on your good sense.
Miserable fool! You seek to extort tribute from China? Be gone, else I shall have you gutted like a pig!
I regret that we are unable to comply with your request at this time.
I wonder: is it madness or deep, abiding stupidity that causes you to make such a demand?
Very well. But we will have our vengeance. I suggest that you sleep with one eye open from now on.
Certainly. China is happy to assist her friends.
Very well. It is probably less expensive than open war.
You are playing a dangerous game.
Very well. The next time I shall not be so polite!
Indeed? I trust that you will not live to regret your short-sightedness.
Consider yourself fortunate that we have let your pitiful civilization survive. Do not try our patience again!

Times have changed. The new world stage is evolving. The people are conflicted. The people are yearning for new prospects at a better life.
Recognizing the potential threat from aliens and other external threats, the XCOM Initiative was born to protect the populace from enemies known, and unknown.
World Congress Becomes League of Nations

The World Congress attempts at development into a League of Nations. International affairs become much more involved and complex. A special session is called to choose the host of this newly-developing League.
League of Nations Becomes United Nations

The League of Nations is reborn as the United Nations. A special session to is called to choose the host of this powerful new diplomatic force. The United Nations will continue as before, but regular sessions will alternate with sessions allowing civilizations to try and claim Global Hegemony, making [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Diplomatic Victory[ENDCOLOR] possible. To enable these sessions, a [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]World Ideology Resolution[ENDCOLOR] must be active.

Leaders and their vassals from around the world meet together in the World Congress to discuss international affairs. City-States enter their place on the world stage and formally enter international diplomacy as independent nations. Their first order of business is to determine who will host the Congress.

The voices of nations large and small fight to be heard and international affairs become more complex. Amidst this development, the World Congress calls a special session to determine the next host of the Congress.

The rapid changes within nations around the world result in equally rapid changes to the international relations between them, prompting the World Congress to adapt to meet new challenges. A special session is called to choose the next host to lead the Congress forward.
