While modern warships bear little resemblance to the earliest galleys, they still keep to the same basic design principles - be capable of destroying the other guy first, before he can take out you.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Frigate[ENDCOLOR], an integral ranged unit in Enlightenment Era navies.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Damn the torpedoes, Full speed ahead!"[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Admiral David Glasgow Farragut[NEWLINE][TAB]

The first experience mankind had with electricity was in the form of shocks from electric fish, recorded by Egyptian authors as far back as 2750 BC. In the 15th century AD, the Arabs discovered that lightning was another form of electricity, and this was later confirmed by a British-American scientist named Ben Franklin in 1752. The first semi-reliable battery was made in 1800 by Alessandro Volta, and in 1821 Michael Faraday invented the electric motor.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Advances in electricity in the second half of the 19th century by geniuses like Nikola Tesla, Thomas Edison, George Westinghouse, Alexander Graham Bell and Lord Kelvin revolutionized life around the world. The telegraph, followed shortly by the telephone and then the radio, radically increased the speed and accuracy with which information could be transmitted. Once a transatlantic cable was laid, a message from New York could reach London in seconds. Before electricity, a message carried on the fastest boat would take weeks. The electric light revolutionized home and workplace, and the phonograph, radio and movie camera did the same for entertainment. The creation of power plants that pushed energy in the form of electricity into people's homes has changed human living conditions almost beyond comprehension. Driven by electricity, the "Second Industrial Revolution" saw the greatest improvement in human life since the printing press.
Grants an additional [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] Trade Route. Also allows Cities to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Stock Exchange[ENDCOLOR], a building which boosts [ICON_GOLD] Gold.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Is it a fact - or have I dreamt it - that, by means of electricity, the world of matter has become a great nerve, vibrating thousands of miles in a breathless point of time?"[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Nathaniel Hawthorne[NEWLINE][TAB]

Electronics covers the branch of technology which studies the controlled motion of electrons through various forms of media, including vacuums. This is not the same as Electrical Technology, which is concerned with the generation and distribution of power. Electronics wasn't recognized as its own field of study until 1950, when it was split off from radio technology.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Electronic circuits can be classified into two distinct groups, analog or digital. Analog circuits are generally simple combinations of basic circuits, utilizing a continuous range of voltage; most modern circuits are rarely ever entirely analog in nature anymore. Digital circuits form the basis of modern computers and programmable logic controllers, as they are the most common physical representation of Boolean algebra (0's and 1's anyone?).[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The study and development of electronics is deeply tied to that of mathematics, and proficiency in the latter is necessary for the former. Creating and analyzing complex circuits involves solving linear systems of multiple unknown variables (like voltage and current at given locations), which is why much of today's circuit design is augmented by design automation software packages, a rather "meta" practice if you get right down to it.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Police Station[ENDCOLOR], increasing City security level.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"There's a basic principle about consumer electronics: it gets more powerful all the time and it gets cheaper all the time."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Trip Hawkins[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB][TAB]

Engineering is the science (or art perhaps) of designing complex materials, structures, devices, and systems. In modern parlance it has a fairly wide reach - bioengineers design cells, software engineers create computer programs, and so forth - but historically the term was applied to the construction of physical stuff, like machines, bridges, railroads, factories, and so forth. (Originally the term "engineer" referred specifically to those who created military engines.)[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Engineering came into its own in the 19th century, as countries around the world embarked on huge construction projects. Completed by the French in 1869, the Suez Canal connected the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea, making it possible to sail from Europe to India without the long and arduous journey around Africa. The United States completed the transcontinental railroad in the same year, and the Brooklyn Bridge was constructed in 1883.

Allows your cities to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Aqueducts[ENDCOLOR], increasing the [ICON_FOOD] Food that is carried over as your city grows. Also allows Workers to construct [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Forts[ENDCOLOR] on map tiles, increasing the defense of units stationed there. Additionally, bridges are automatically added to roads which cross rivers, allowing units to pass over them without slowing down.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Instrumental or mechanical science is the noblest and, above all others, the most useful."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Leonardo da Vinci[NEWLINE][TAB]

The Renaissance Age of Exploration was initiated by the Portuguese under the leadership of Henry the Navigator. Relying on the Caravel, the Portuguese pushed south down the west coast of Africa, eventually rounding the Cape of Good Hope into the Indian Ocean. By Christopher Columbus' voyage of 1492, the focus had changed to finding a western route to the riches of China and the Indies. Spain would take the lead for the next half century, achieving the first circumnavigation of the globe (in a voyage led -- but not survived -- by Ferdinand Magellan) and the conquest of many of the native civilizations of the Americas.

Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Caravel[ENDCOLOR], an expensive naval unit that represents a major expedition of New World exploration. Build these and sail them to the western map edge to gain VP.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"We shall not cease from exploration, and the end of all our exploring will be to arrive where we started and know the place for the first time."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - T. S. Eliot[NEWLINE][TAB]

Fertilizer is a substance that feeds and speeds the growth of plants. Fertilizer has been around for as long as human civilization, dating back to the time when the first farmer realized that grass grew taller where the oxen had pooped. From that point on farmers have been collecting animal by-products and applying them to the soil, increasing the crop yield, especially from fields that have been farmed continuously for generations and thus have been stripped of most nutrients.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Fertilizers generally contain nitrogen, phosphorous, and potassium as their active ingredients. While historically most of the fertilizers have been organic and animal-based, many modern fertilizers are actually mined from beneath the earth's surface or chemically manufactured in vast factories.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]As the world's population has increased, so has the need for ever more potent fertilizers, and today's farms are far more productive than at any other time in history. However, this productivity has come at a price: rainwater from farms carries the fertilizer into streams and rivers, causing explosive growth in certain microorganisms which grow so fast they almost literally choke the life out of the waterway. Also, many modern fertilizers are created at least in part from petrochemicals, and their price can fluctuate dramatically along with the price of oil. In short, fertilizers are extremely useful and can greatly increase the world's food supply, but care must be taken to ensure that they don't do more harm to the environment than good.
Increases the [ICON_FOOD] Food from Farmed tiles without Fresh Water, providing a massive boost to growth.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The nation that destroys its soil destroys itself."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Franklin Delano Roosevelt[NEWLINE][TAB]

Throughout history, man has dreamed of conquering the skies. Leonardo da Vinci's visions of flight are well-known, of course, and there were many other lesser visionaries as well. The early theorists looked at the natural masters of the air, birds, and they proposed machines that emulated their wing shape and flapping motions (ornithopters). But the early designers lacked the materials, engines, and knowledge of aerodynamics to bring their visions to life.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The study of aerodynamics was advanced over the 16th, 17th, 18th and 19th centuries by brilliant scientists like da Vinci, Galileo, Huygens, Newton, Bernoulli, Euler and Smeaton. In 1804 Englishman George Cayley flew a fixed-wing glider model, and in 1853 he created a full-scale model which carried his (reluctant) coachman in the first known manned glider flight.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In 1902 the Wright brothers constructed their own glider with an advanced wing shape. Unable to find an experienced manufacturer to construct a light gasoline-powered engine to their specifications, they designed and built their own. On December 17, 1903 the Wright flyer flew four times, at distances up to 852 feet. The years following the Wright brothers' breakthrough saw huge and rapid improvements in the technology of flying. By 1908 American Glenn Hammond Curtiss flew over 1 kilometer (approx. six tenths of a mile), and in 1909 Frenchman Louis Bleriot flew across the English Channel.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]World War I saw huge advances in flight technology, especially in the weaponization of the air, with the creation of fighters and bombers. By the '20s pilots were regularly flying across the continents, and in 1927 Charles Lindberg completed the first nonstop solo flight across the Atlantic Ocean. World War II saw tremendous improvements in the speed, range, durability, and killing power of aircraft, and by the end of the war jet planes, continent-spanning high-altitude bombers and helicopters were in service.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In the modern era, air travel has become commonplace, with a journey from the United States to China - an impossible dream only 75 years ago - being now seen as notable mostly for its tediousness. And although the airborn terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001 have made air travel slightly more perilous, millions of people around the world still take to the air every day. Flight is here to stay.

Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Triplane[ENDCOLOR], an Air Unit designed to gain control of the skies, and the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Bomber[ENDCOLOR], which can devastate Land Units and Cities. Also allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Paratrooper[ENDCOLOR], a late-game infantry unit capable of paradropping behind enemy lines.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Aeronautics was neither an industry nor a science. It was a miracle."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Igor Sikorsky[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB][TAB]

It's difficult to write a "history" for technology that hasn't actually been discovered yet. But here are some possible big breakthroughs that might dramatically alter the human condition. Sooner or later, medicine will figure out how to cure cancer and other diseases, dramatically increase human life, and directly interface the human brain with machines. Cheap, clean forms of energy will be discovered. Computers will get faster and smaller. Games will get more immersive and realistic. Nasty new weapons will be invented. And a giant killer death robot will be created to destroy all life on the planet, but we will be saved by an army of mutant kung fu cyborgs. The future will indeed be interesting!
A repeating technology that increases your score and grants 1 [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness in every City each time it is researched.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"I think we agree, the past is over."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - George W. Bush[NEWLINE][TAB]

Orbital production is a concept that encompasses the cultivation, purification, manufacture, and production of various biological and non-biological raw materials in Earth orbit. It crosses the boundaries of scientific research and the commercial space industry, and presents a wide range of application possibilities for production systems in space environments.
Later in the game, you can build X-COM, a powerful recon unit. It can also create orbital refineries and orbital food-growing facilities that provide production and nanomaterials.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The tricky thing about adamantium is, that if you ever manage to process its raw, liquid form, you got to keep it that way, keep it hot. Because once the metal cools, it's indestructible."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - X-Men[NEWLINE][TAB]

Artifical intelligence is the intelligence exhibited by machines and software. Although technically any intelligent agent is one that can perceive its environment and undertake actions that maximize its chances of success, colloquially the term refers to a machine or software that displays a notable degree of self-awareness and sentience, displaying a human-like level of intelligence. With the development of "smart" devices and other forms of cognitive technology, achieving this goal becomes a possibility, although there are some concerns that, as such intelligences may not think in a truly "human" fashion, they may become rivals or otherwise hostile towards humanity. Still, as intelligent behavior may be defined as being logical or human-like, it is also possible such new intelligences would be benevolent or friendly towards humanity, so long as humanity acted intelligently themselves.
Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]AI Networks[ENDCOLOR], which increase [ICON_RESEARCH] Science and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"I think, therefore I am"[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Rene Descartes[NEWLINE][TAB]

The term 'arcology' is a portmaneteau of the words 'architecture' and 'ecology', and is a vision of architectural design principles for very densely populated habitats. An arcology is distinguished from a merely large building in that it is designed to lessen the impact of human habitation on any given ecosystem. Adapting to life within an arcology would likely require social and cultural adaptation as well, with an increased emphasis on frugality and shared social resources, and a lessening of private space.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Aerospace Complexes[ENDCOLOR], which increase the air capacity of a City, [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Orbital Habitats[ENDCOLOR], which increase [ICON_FOOD] Food, and the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Central Command[ENDCOLOR], which improves Information Hubs, Distribution Hubs, and Metroplex Hubs across the empire. Also allows Workers to construct [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Arcologies[ENDCOLOR], which provide [ICON_FOOD] Food and [ICON_GOLD] Gold.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Architecture is the physical form of the ecology of the human, the configuration of matter which allows for the best energetic and willful flux"[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Paolo Soleri[NEWLINE][TAB]

Manned exploration and inhabitation of outer space will require significant advances in the technologies available to sustain humans in one of the most hostile environment possible. In particular, self-sustaining environments that can provide breathable atmosphere, drinkable water, and food will be needed. These technologies will not be applicable only to space travel, however, as it will enable us to create self-contained environments underground, in arid regions, or under the ocean, greatly increasing the volume of space available for human habitation.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Vertical Farms[ENDCOLOR] and [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Hydroponics Domes[ENDCOLOR] in order to increase [ICON_FOOD] Food output, as well as [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Geofronts[ENDCOLOR] to improve city defense.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The more artificial a human environment becomes, the more the word 'natural' becomes a term of value."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Wendell Berry[NEWLINE][TAB]

The application of celestial mechanics to practical matters concerning orbital flight development and interstellar mapping lately has become one of the most vital topics of research for space exploration. As the colonists contemplated a return to space, astrodynamics – founded on the ancient laws of Newton and Kepler – laid out the unvarying formulae of free, circular, elliptical, parabolic and hyperbolic orbits. But advances in design and energy sources, coupled with the differences in mass and rotational period of this planet compared to Old Earth, meant that velocities and orbital periods could be increased and shortened respectively. Soon enough, satellites of every sort circled overhead. This in turn triggered a new interest in the “geography” of near space among the Earth; the result was a plentitude of new planetariums and research grants devoted to the heavens as many felt manned space missions would occur within their lifetime.
Astrodynamics allows space navigation, “Space Surveillance Network”

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"I never cease to find beauty in the fact that even though we walk among the stars, we still hold them in awe."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Samatar Jama Barre, This is Not Exile[NEWLINE][TAB]

As cognitive technology advanced, fully autonomous mechanical systems became increasingly feasible. While not fully sentient or self-aware, these systems were capable of sufficiently complex decision-making that they could handle unexpected circumstances. This allowed human operators to provide simpler instructions and commands, and mechanical systems required less oversight, making them increasingly practical in real-world environments rather than controlled settings.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Advanced Destroyers[ENDCOLOR], the most powerful naval melee unit, as well as [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Drone Hives[ENDCOLOR] which provide [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_GOLD] Gold, and the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Borehole[ENDCOLOR], which improves Geothermal Plants and Mines. Also allows Workers to construct [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Support Nodes[ENDCOLOR], which provide [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_GOLD] Gold, and heal nearby units each turn.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Never do anything yourself that others can do for you."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Agatha Christie, The Labours of Hercules[NEWLINE][TAB]

While the term "gengineering" refers to the creation of entirely new organisms through genetic manipulation, biomodification reflects taking existing organisms and modifying them to improve their capabilities in various ways. In particular, modification of the human genome allows the adaptation of individuals to augmented forms that can meet a variety of needs, whether it be strength and durability in combat, or the ability to work in hazardous environments. As biomodfication becomes increasingly prevalent, more environments become available to humans to live and work, although the definition of what constitutes being "human" starts to become blurred.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Biotroopers[ENDCOLOR], the most powerful genetically-engineered infantry, as well as [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Bioenhancement Centres[ENDCOLOR] which increase the production of Mutants and Chimeras, and provide newly created units with unique promotions, as well as [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Genejack Facilities[ENDCOLOR], which increase [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"As human beings, our only sensible scale of values is one based on lessening the agony of existence."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - H.P. Lovecraft[NEWLINE][TAB]

The advancing study of biology and medicine lead to the creation of methods for artifical gestation, and manipulation of organisms on a cellular level. Once the ability to incubate organisms artifically in a laboratory environment was achieved, attention was turned to the capability to replicate particularly useful organisms, eventually leading to the search for some means to replicate an actual human being. Still, while it is possible to replicate an organism genetically, that organism may not mature into an identical twin of its predecssor, due to environmental influences.
Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Clone Labs[ENDCOLOR] and [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Aquaculture Labs[ENDCOLOR], which enhance nearby resources.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Why would you clone people when you can go to bed with them and make a baby? C'mon, it's stupid."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Ray Bradbury[NEWLINE][TAB]

As the capability to produce increasingly small-scale devices develops, so has the capacity to integrate computer systems into practically any item or material, and with the development of networked computing, allows appliances or other objects to be made increasingly "smart". A smart home, for example, can monitor activity in various rooms, adjusting lighting or temperature as needed to conserve power. Smart appliances can monitor usage and even determine when to place orders for new food or other supplies as needed. Furthermore, even simple "smart" systems acting in concert can display increasingly intelligent emergent behavior.

Combining automation systems and cognitive engineering can produce offensive robots and arsenal ships. Network hubs can be installed to strengthen sub-connections between cities. Virtua Idol World Wonders can be built.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Digital behavior is just a replication of human behavior."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Paul Papadimitriou[NEWLINE][TAB]

Computronium is a material hypothesized by Norman Margolus and Tommaso Toffoli of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology to be used as "programmable matter," a substrate for computer modeling of virtually any real object.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Spaceship Cockpit[ENDCOLOR], which is one of the spaceship components required for the Science Victory.
[NEWLINE][ TAB ][ TAB ]"Men are only as good as their technical development allows them to be."[NEWLINE][ TAB ][ TAB ] - George Orwell [NEWLINE][ TAB ]

Although cybernetics as a science is broadly concerned the study of systems of any nature which are capable of receiving, storing, and processing information so as to use it for control, its study of the connection between stimulus and action lends itself to the common perception of the study of interfaces between humans and machines, and how mechanical sensors and agents might be integrated with human decision-making processes. However, cybernetics can also be applied to such things as purely mechanical systems (studying artificial intelligence and emergent behavior), as well as biological and social systems.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Hovertanks[ENDCOLOR], the most advanced mobile unit in the game, as well as [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Telepresence Hubs[ENDCOLOR], which increase [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_GOLD] Gold.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The world of the future will be an even more demanding struggle against the limitations of our intelligence, not a comfortable hammock in which we can lie down to be waited upon by our robot slaves." -- Norbert Weiner[NEWLINE][TAB]

With the proliferation of artificial intelligences, as well as the advancement of cybernetics allowing humans to utilize mind-machine interfaces and telepresence, the concept of the mind and personality being linked to one's physical body becomes increasingly outmoded. Advances in computer networks and technology allow people to project themselves anywhere on the planet, or perceive entirely artifical worlds. Ultimately, such a society may discard concerns about the physical world, with identity being determined solely by one's mind, rather than one's body, and one's perceptions may be determined largely by one's interactions with the electronic environment humanity lives in.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Brain Uploading Facilities[ENDCOLOR], which increase [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, [ICON_RESEARCH] Science, [ICON_GOLD] Gold, and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture but reduce population.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"If you stay right where you are, then people will eventually come to you."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Robert Doisneau[NEWLINE][TAB]

While environmentalism has been a social movement concerned with the preservation of nature against human activity, it does also have the drawback of regarding both "nature" and "humanity" as separate and distinct from each other. As the study of ecological systems progresses, increasing movements that seek to view both humans and their environment more holistically start to develop, encouraging people to view themselves as part of a single, unified system. Some of the more radical proponents of these new ecological philosophies (or "ecosophies") advocate that thought should be given to modifying both humans and the environment so they can live in greater harmony with each other -- with competing needs, simply preserving both humanity and the environment as they are is likely to lead to further conflict.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Ecosanctuaries[ENDCOLOR] which provide [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness and [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Biofactories[ENDCOLOR] which provide [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_GOLD] Gold.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Every living being is connected intimately, and from this intimacy follows the capacity of identification and as its natural consequences, practice of non-violence."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Arne Næss[NEWLINE][TAB]

The human investigation of the principles under which the universe operates have lead to investigations of the functioning of the universe at the smallest and most high-energy states. The most evident products of this research can be found in the extended exploration and development of the solar system, resulting in powerful booster engines capable of propelling spacecraft between interplanetary colonies, as well as facilitating the development of new generations of space stations and bases on other worlds.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Spaceship Boosters[ENDCOLOR], one of the spaceship components required for the Science Victory, as well as the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Spaceship Factory[ENDCOLOR] and [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Moon Base[ENDCOLOR].
[NEWLINE][ TAB ][ TAB ]"If you want to find the secrets of the universe, think in terms of energy, frequency and vibration."[NEWLINE][ TAB ][ TAB ] - Nikola Tesla [NEWLINE][ TAB ]

The increasing awareness of ecological systems and how they work has, in turn, lead to concerns about the impact of human activity upon them. Environmentalism is a broad social movement that emphasizes environmental protection and the health of the environment. It advocates for the lawful preservation, restoration, and improvement of the natural environment, and typically seeks to control pollution and encourage natural diversity.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Geothermal Plants[ENDCOLOR] and [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Tidal Plants[ENDCOLOR], which increase [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production. Also allows Workers to construct [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Nature Preserves[ENDCOLOR], which provide [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_GOLD] Gold.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"We have lived our lives by the assumption that what was good for us would be good for the world. We have been wrong. We must change our lives so that it will be possible to live by the contrary assumption, that what is good for the world will be good for us. And that requires that we make the effort to know the world and learn what is good for it." -- Wendell Berry[NEWLINE][TAB]

The science concerned with establishing the optimum living conditions for humans, animals and plants, especially through proper provisioning and environment. If Facism is your ideology, Eugenics will improve the genetic quality of a human population, enhancing individual traits, in favor of certain group membership.

You can build clonetroopers and eco-friendly villages using AND fungus. You can construct a fungal agronomic laboratory that can utilize ADN fungus and a building that increases the production of the ocean.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"People used to say to my friend Mary, a quadriplegic, 'You still have your mind.' She would say, 'I still have my body.' The world tells me to divorce myself from my flesh, to live in my head... I don't want to be fleshless."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Anne Finger[NEWLINE][TAB]

The development and launch of artificial satellites has brought great advances in science and technology, particularly in space development. These technological advances did not simply push the boundaries of science, but served to enhance our understanding of the world and the universe. These technological leaps have also contributed significantly to the development and production of intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs). The technology of ICBMs is complex in itself and requires technological leaps in many of the areas that make it possible. Advanced physics, materials science, electromagnetics, and control systems are all critical factors in the design and implementation of these advanced weapon systems. Technological advances in these areas can be applied not only to ICBMs, but also to other types of missiles, spacecraft, and aircraft.
Can produce intercontinental ballistic missiles. Enhanced Operational Ability increases the abilities of Generals and Admirals. It can produce futuristic infantry power armor prostheses.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"We cannot become what we need to be, remaining what we are."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Max De Pree[NEWLINE][TAB]

While the genetic modification of the human genome holds the most promise for human augmentation, it is a highly complex endeavor as the human genome is the product of millions of years of evolution. A simpler undertaking is to take much simpler genomes, such as those found in plants and animals, in order to modify them more drastically -- or even produce entirely new genomes. In time, experimentation with genetic manipulation lead to the capability to craft and engineer entirely new organisms, leading to the term "gengineering", a portmanetau of the term "genetic engineering". With the capbility to engineer living organisms to fill specific ecological niches and other roles, it becomes increasingly possible to manipulate the environment to meet particular needs or desires.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Chimeras[ENDCOLOR], genetically engineered combat units, as well as [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Biogenesis pods[ENDCOLOR] which increase the production of Mutants and Chimeras, and provide newly created units with unique promotions.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"If you realize that all things change, there is nothing you will try to hold on to. If you are not afraid of dying, there is nothing you cannot achieve."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Lao Tzu, Tao Te Ching[NEWLINE][TAB]

With the discovery of DNA, and the increasing ability to manipulate organisms on a genetic level, it was inevitable that some would investigate the effects of manipulating the genetic composition of organisms, in an effort to improve them in various ways. Genetic manipulation can be highly problematic, however, as even simpler organisms that have been genetically modified may prove to have unintended biological and environmental effects. The possibility of human genetic modification is an issue with many social and ethical concerns, although some feel the potential benefits would outweigh such risks.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Mutants[ENDCOLOR], a cheap infantry unit that can heal itself, as well as [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Gene Labs[ENDCOLOR], which provide a bonus to certain resources, as well as increasing the production of [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"We cannot become what we need to be, remaining what we are."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Max De Pree[NEWLINE][TAB]

The advancement of computing systems has increasingly resulted in their distribution across a wider network of computers. Parallel processing allows computations to be conducted more quickly, as various calaculations can be carried out simultaneously, while distributed computer networks create systems that are more flexible and resilient against mechanical failure, as they are no longer limited to single machines.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Vertols[ENDCOLOR], a hovering military unit, and [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Arsenal Ships[ENDCOLOR], a futuristic ranged naval unit, as well as [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Research Servers[ENDCOLOR] which increase [ICON_RESEARCH] Science and [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Autoplants[ENDCOLOR] which increase [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"All of a sudden, we've lost a lot of control. We can't turn off our internet; we can't turn off our smartphones; we can't turn off our computers." -- Steve Wozniak[NEWLINE][TAB]

With the full maturation of both biomodfication and cybernetics, it becomes possible to augment the human body in almost limitless ways. Human beings can be stronger, smarter, live longer and be relatively free from disease or injury. While there are ethical and even logistical concerns with such human augmentation, it would leave humanity poised to transcend its limitations.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Spaceship Stasis Chamber[ENDCOLOR], which is one of the spaceship components required for the Science Victory.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"I teach you the Overman. Man is something which shall be surpassed."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Friedrich Nietzsche[NEWLINE][TAB]

With the development of both genetic biomodification and cybernetics, limitless possibilities for human augmentation became possible. Virtually any component of the human body could be replaced with a vat-grown or cybernetic replacement. Eventually, however, some began to see baseline humanity as the limitation, as it could only accept so much modification, and more experimentation began on establishing improved versions of the human genome.
Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Birthing Pods[ENDCOLOR], which increase [ICON_RESEARCH] Science and [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production.

[NEWLINE][ TAB ][ TAB ]"Mind you, I've always wondered if Kei wasn't one of those Yamashita upgrades -- you know, with too much adrenocorticotropic hormone, too little monoamine oxidase?"[NEWLINE][ TAB ][ TAB ] - Adam Warren, A Plague of Angels [NEWLINE][ TAB ]

Expanding upon the concept of the arcology towards urban development, advances in materials engineering and other technologies may someday make it feasible to accomplish tremendous feats of engineering -- housing an entire city of people in a single structure, designed to optimize human comfort and society while minimizing their impact on the surrounding environment. Such a structure would be a tremendous accomplishment, and would undoubtably have an equally great impact upon human society.
Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Crawlers[ENDCOLOR], the most powerful siege unit, as well as [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Metroplex Hubs[ENDCOLOR], which provide [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
[NEWLINE][ TAB ][ TAB ]"Men have become the tools of their tools"[NEWLINE][ TAB ][ TAB ] - David Thoreau [NEWLINE][ TAB ]

Implants are man-made devices that are implanted or grafted to living tissue. They came in a wide range of types and effects, and would most likely work like mutations, but are artifacts that must be surgically implanted to the host's body. While there are some concerns about the ethics of using these implants, they do prove to be increasingly valuable and useful, whether in enhancing the productivity and effectiveness of workers, or in making more powerful soldiers for the battlefield.

Prosthetic transplants allow fast walking, bio-enhanced infantry with excellent body regeneration, and mutant diplomats invisible to external enemies. You can also build implant parlors to strengthen your ground units. Installing an Apex Center will enhance your spy's abilities and give you a great diplomat.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Revelations, the Bible[NEWLINE][TAB]

Mechatronics, developed in the early stages of the 21st Century, is an interdisciplinary, synergistic melding of electrical and computer engineering, telecommunications and control systems in mechanical design. It allows for advanced automation in “dumb” machines. Programmed in repetitive patterns free of expensive oversight, mechatronics allows for inexpensive, efficient automated production facilities of basic consumer items. Things like furnishings, clothing, hand tools … indeed, anything without elaborate moving parts … can be produced in large quantities with minimal human involvement. An offshoot of mechatronics is the field of bio-mechatronics, which seeks to integrate mechanical parts with a human body, usually in the form of removable items such as powered myoelectric prostheses or exoskeletons.
Mechatronics allows for the development of remotely operated machinery and robotics, including the mobile and ballistic LEV units.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Machines can be journeymen to machine apprentices, as long as we are still the masters."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Hutama, We are All Destined to Prosper[NEWLINE][TAB]

Memetics is the study of the development and spread of memes -- self-contained units that carry cultural ideas, symbols, or practices that can be transmitted from one mind to another. They are considered by some to be a cultural analogue to genes, in the way they replicate, mutate, and respond to selective pressures. The study of memetics may help us understand how societies and cultures develop and evolve over time, although some suggest it may ultimately also help people manipulate and shape socieities into more desirable forms.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Entertainment Servers[ENDCOLOR], which increase [ICON_CULTURE] Culture output, and [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]VR Training Centres[ENDCOLOR] to help train veteran units. Also allows Workers to construct [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Eco-Communes[ENDCOLOR], which provide [ICON_FOOD] Food, [ICON_CULTURE] Culture, and [ICON_GOLD] Gold.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Not even the most heavily-armed police state can exert brute force to all of its citizens all of the time. Meme management is so much subtler; the rose-tinted refraction of perceived reality, the contagious fear of threatening alternatives."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Peter Watts, Blindsight[NEWLINE][TAB]

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Infinities and indivisibles transcend our finite understanding, the former on account of their magnitude, the latter because of their smallness; Imagine what they are when combined."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Galileo Galilei[NEWLINE][TAB]

Nanomaterials research takes a materials science-based approach to nanotechnology, leveraging advances in materials metrology and synthesis which have been developed in support of microfabrication research. Materials with structure at the nanoscale often have unique optical, electronic, or mechanical properties.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Power Armor Infantry[ENDCOLOR], a futuristic infantry unit, and [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Nanomaterial Plants[ENDCOLOR] which provide Nanomaterials. Also allows Workers to construct [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Generators[ENDCOLOR], which provide [ICON_GOLD] Gold.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Carbon atoms on a distant planet rearranged themselves into DNA, microorganisms formed, grew backbones, swam around the ocean, mutated into amphibians and crawled onto dry land — and finally a cab appeared at the mouth of the alley."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Mark Coggins, "The Immortal Game"[NEWLINE][TAB]
Build powerful railgun tanks that use nanomaterials.

As machines have become increasingly sophisticated, the interfaces required to interact with them have as well. Being able to control a machine with one's thoughts as an extension of one's body would be an incredible achievement, making it far simpler to perform complex tasks with mechanical assistance. However, the brain is itself a highly complex organ, and achieving a direct interface a significant challenge. Still, progress is being made in establishing connections between computers and other technological devices and human nerves, allowing both motor control and sensory input of technological devices.
Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Cybersubs[ENDCOLOR], the most advanced submarine unit.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"A picture is worth a thousand words. An interface is worth a thousand pictures."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Ben Shneiderman[NEWLINE][TAB]

Ultra-precise uranium laser enrichment is a highly precise technique used in the enrichment process for uranium. This technique is based on the principle of selectively ionizing and separating specific isotopes of uranium atoms using a laser. By selectively ionizing isotopes using a laser, the required isotopes can be concentrated more efficiently and precisely.

Hydrogen fusion bombs can be made by producing plutonium through the Aperture Enrichment Center and hyperenrichment. Uranium can be obtained from nuclear fuel reprocessing facilities. In addition, develop your city by building hubs.

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Nuclear power will help provide the electricity our growing economy needs without increasing emissions. It is a truly environmentally responsible energy source." [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]- Michael Burgess[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]

While national governments still have the most resources to invest in space exploration, commercial enterprises have become increasingly interested in the opportunities of privatized access to space. Either way, orbital development holds opportunities for both research and industrial production, as well as helping facilitate and maintain increasingly complex orbital communication networks.

You can develop space by building a spaceship factory and a spaceship launch facility. Through related research, it is possible to produce defensive ground units called battle suits. In order to adapt to the external environment, technology for alternative meat factories has also developed.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The exploration and use of outer space,including the moon and other celestial bodies, shall be carried out for the benefit and in the interests of all countries, irrespective of their degree of economic or scientific development, and shall be the province of all mankind."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Article 1 of the Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, Including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies[NEWLINE][TAB]

As the methods of genetic manipulation become increasingly refined, the possibiilty of using genetics to produce more effective organs and organic components increases. While the wholescale manipulation of the human genome would produce more effective results, the sheer complexity of the task makes it easier to focus on engineering organic components to specific standards, even if the rest of the host body suffers significant problems. While there are some concerns about the ethics of using these engineered host bodies to incubate augmented organs, they do prove to be increasingly valuable and useful, whether in enhancing the productivity and effectiveness of workers, or in making more powerful soldiers for the battlefield.
You can build reinforced body infantry and hybird drones.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Life is an inherently depreciating asset."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Suzanne Marjorie Fielding, Transplanetary Management, Methods, and Resources[NEWLINE][TAB]

From the crude coal-fired electrical generators to the massive “sunscoop,” the production of Energy on Old Earth was a race against demand and dwindling resources. On this planet, plentiful sources, traditional or unexpected, for the production of Energy to feed the needs of the growing colonies exist. It was only a matter of those first colonial engineers discovering how to extract and utilize those sources, constructing innovative power plants and transmission systems; utilizing a variety of methods, colonial survival is a testament to their success in doing so. Even today research into sustainable power systems is critical if we are to avoid the Energy crises that plagued distant Earth.
Oil can be extracted from wheat resources. Build generators to strengthen towns, industrial parks and advanced energy research parks.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The necessity of an artificial power source is a myth. An ecosystem powers itself. When humanity learns to live in harmony with its surroundings, we will reap the same benefits of power."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Daoming Sochua, Scientific Morality Vol.VII[NEWLINE][TAB]

The planetary migration plan is a long-term plan for humankind to move to another planet or celestial body to maintain and develop life. The plan aims to expand future viability, supplement Earth's resources, and promote new scientific discoveries and technological advances.
Build an Orbital Refinery to obtain nanomaterials. Orbital incubators can be used to enhance space stations. You can produce Space Marines, very powerful defense units.

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Having a self-contained base on Mars is important because Mars is far enough away from Earth that (in case of war) it has a better chance of survival than a lunar base. If I don not build a self-sustaining city on Mars, I will consider it a failure in my lifetime." [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]-Elon MUSK[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]

The development of nanomaterials derived from rare resource exploration has shown that it is possible to manipulate materials at the molecular and atomic level to create new materials and structures. The next challenge in finding true nanotechnology is to produce real working components (power sources, motors and other mechanical parts) at this scale so that nanoscale machines can do the work. Increasingly sophisticated tools are devised to manipulate molecules at the nanoscale, making sophisticated and futuristic materials much more common and usable.

It will enable deep-sea mining and exploration of the Earth, enabling production in many cities and nanomaterials in the ocean. Hills and mountains can also be explored for minerals, increasing the city's output.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Infinities and indivisibles transcend our finite understanding, the former on account of their magnitude, the latter because of their smallness; Imagine what they are when combined."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Galileo Galilei[NEWLINE][TAB]

The culimination of nanotechnology would be the development of "smart materials" -- materials that are actually comprised of intelligent nanomachines, capable of adapting themselves to their environments or other stimuli. Nanomachines like these, working in concert, would allow humans to have complete control over their environments -- construction shelters or other objects upon demand. Depending on the nature and distribution of the nanomachines, they could also serve other roles, such as personal defense or even transportation.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Nexus[ENDCOLOR] units, a powerful carrier and support unit, as well as the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Utility Fog[ENDCOLOR], which improves city defense and increases [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Everything changes, nothing remains without change."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Siddhārtha Gautama[NEWLINE][TAB]

Humanity has always felt an underlying desire to explore and expand, to find what lies beyond the horizon. Outer space provides the ultimate frontier, a broad expanse that humanity can expand into and explore. The achievement of a level of technology that would permit humans to travel to another star system may be as pivotal in human history as the development of the first tools.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Spaceship Engine[ENDCOLOR], which is one of the spaceship components required for the Science Victory.
[NEWLINE][ TAB ][ TAB ]"There is no easy way to the stars from the earth."[NEWLINE][ TAB ][ TAB ] - Seneca [NEWLINE][ TAB ]

A supercomputer is a computer with a high-level computational capacity compared to a general-purpose computer.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Supercomputers were introduced in the 1960s and the first supercomputers only used a few processors. In the 1990s, machines with thousands of processors began to appear and, by the end of the 20th century, massively parallel supercomputers with tens of thousands of "off-the-shelf" processors were the norm.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Supercomputers play an important role in the field of computational science, and are used for a wide range of computationally intensive tasks in various fields, including quantum mechanics, weather forecasting, climate research, oil and gas exploration, molecular modeling (computing the structures and properties of chemical compounds, biologicalmacromolecules, polymers, and crystals), and physical simulations (such as simulations of the early moments of the universe, airplane and spacecraft aerodynamics, the detonation of nuclear weapons, and nuclear fusion) and would eventualy leads to the Digital revolution, also knows as the 4th industrial revolution that has been occurring since the middle of the last century. It is characterized by a fusion of technologies that is blurring the lines between the physical, digital, and biological spheres that include technologies like artifical intelligence, augmented reality, virtual reality, blockchain, cryptocurrency, 3D printers, big data, robotics, etc... As the physical, digital, and biological worlds continue to converge, new technologies and platforms will increasingly enable citizens to engage with governments, voice their opinions, coordinate their efforts, and even circumvent the supervision of public authorities. Simultaneously, governments will gain new technological powers to increase their control over populations, based on pervasive surveillance systems and the ability to control digital infrastructure, would profoundly impact the nature of national and international security, affecting both the probability and the nature of conflict.

You can build e-commerce servers that increase your city's gold output. You can build a cyber police station to increase your city's security. You can build a communication base station that informs city landmarks, towns, etc. You can produce UAVs that navigate your borders to establish your first line of defense.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"We cannot become what we need to be, remaining what we are."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Max De Pree[NEWLINE][TAB]

Superconducting-Plasma Energy Mechanics is an innovative field of study created through the combination of superconducting and plasma technologies. Research in this field has developed a technology that generates a strong magnetic field and uses it to control plasma. This field of study has revolutionized the way we produce energy. The use of superconducting-plasma energy dynamics allows stable control of fusion reactions, which can be a powerful means of providing safe and efficient energy. This made it possible to control the plasma and maintain a high energy state, enabling efficient generation of fusion energy. Additionally, this technology has been used in the research and development of high-speed electromagnetic flight vehicles. This enables a high degree of energy efficiency and high power output, which has been used to make spacecraft faster than ever before. Finally, the technology of superconducting-plasma energy mechanics also had an impact on weapon systems. Plasma-powered weapons have great destructive power, which has brought about a great change in military strategy. Superconducting-plasma energy dynamics is expected to play a pivotal role in future technological development, which is expected to greatly change our lives in many ways.

You can build high-speed railways in your city, with walking self-propelled artillery and magnetic levitation trains available to help you attack the city. Plasma bombers and fighters can be mass produced. In addition, the quantum mechanical part has been improved, so it can be developed into various modules within the space station.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Physics is the only profession in which prophecy is not only accurate but routine."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Neil deGrasse Tyson[NEWLINE][TAB]

Dielectric acceleration is the pinnacle of life science, and humanity has challenged the realm of the gods. It is used to accelerate species evolution or to create new species. This scientific approach further enhances strategic depth on the battlefield, helping players create powerful units with special abilities. This technology is used in two main ways. First, "genetic enhancement" improves the genes of existing creatures, enhancing their abilities. It enhances characteristics such as health, speed, and intelligence, and the enhanced unit brings many advantages in battle. Second, "Gene Creation" is a way of creating new creatures, creating new units with unique combat-specific abilities. This can be seen as the ultimate tool created by mankind to challenge the realm of the gods.
You can produce genoswarms that move quickly and harass opponents, and biodrones, the ultimate recon unit.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Man does not weave this web of life. He is merely a strand of it. Whatever he does to the web, he does to himself."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Chief Seattle[NEWLINE][TAB]

As the technology to clone existing organisms matured, it also permitted the increasing development of new, genetically modified organisms that incorporated previously nonexistent traits that could breed true in future generations. Most transgenic organisms could only grow and develop under controlled environments, such as specialized plant nurseries, but new ecotheories helped scientists understand the complex interactions in ecologies and environments, allowing more stable transgenic organisms that could survive in open environments without upsetting the existing ecological balance.

You can build a genetic research complex to increase production, gold, and food output. Increases the gold output of ranches, fishing boats, farms, and camps. You can produce mutated units with great resilience.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Nothing is so painful to the human mind as a great and sudden change."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Mary Shelley, Frankenstein[NEWLINE][TAB]

Not a technology or field of study, globalization describes a process by which different regional economies, cultures, languages, information, and whole societies become integrated into a larger, consolidated network. While often used just to describe economic tendencies in the world market, globalization does take into account everything from migration patterns to the spread of technology and information. While not recognized as a concept until much later, globalization has been around as early as the first trade routes that were created between distant cities.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]One of the earliest definitions of globalization was given by an American entrepreneur Charles Taze Russell in 1897, but it wasn't until the 1960's that the word really entered common parlance. The concept of globalization has been a driving force to both private and public sectors, with large banks opening branches across the world and separate governments joining together under one banner like the United Nations.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Modern globalization has worked to break down both trade and political barriers between differing nations, in order to increase personal independence and prosperity. It promotes free trade and the elimination of tariffs, consolidation of intellectual property laws, a more open sharing of news and information, and freer movement for international travel, tourism, and immigration.

Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]SS Cockpit[ENDCOLOR], a component necessary to win a [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Science Victory[ENDCOLOR]. With Globalization, each Spy you send to another Civilization as a [ICON_DIPLOMAT] Diplomat will increase the number of Delegates you control in the World Congress, bringing you closer to [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Diplomatic Victory[ENDCOLOR].
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The new electronic interdependence recreates the world in the image of a global village."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Marshall McLuhan[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB][TAB]
How can a great scientist help with research?

A Great Scientist can give you a considerable boost towards your next tech, or the unit can be expended to construct an Academy improvement, which provides beakers per turn when the tile is worked. See the section on Great People for more details.

In pre-industrial cities, craftsmen tended to form associations - or trade guilds - based upon their profession; these guilds were intended to both protect craft secrets as well as promote the influence and income of the craftsmen. Predecessors of the trade guilds were found as early as the 3rd Century BC in Rome and Han China. By 300 AD, the practice of craftsmen banding together had spread into Gupta India and Ptolemaic Egypt. In the Middle Ages, guild organizations spread rapidly from Italy throughout Europe; 12th Century records in Paris and London each list over 100 guilds chartered by the cities. In some cases, so powerful were some guilds that they became the governing body of cities, indicated by the guildhalls found in Germany, Switzerland and Holland.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Over time, the guilds took on the task of safeguarding quality and of instruction in the craft, with a life-long progression from apprentice to grandmaster. To insure product quality, the system of trademarks indicating that the item had passed both guild and government standards evolved. However, over time the influence and power of the guilds declined as they fragmented with the coming of new trades, government concerns, and mass production methods. In France, for instance, the guilds were abolished in 1791 AD by the Le Chapelier Law; other countries followed soon did the same. Although largely supplanted by unions in the Industrial Age, there are still examples of guilds in existence, notably in the realms of film, literature and other artistic professions.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Customs House[ENDCOLOR] and [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]East India Company[ENDCOLOR], improving [ICON_GOLD] Gold in your cities.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The merchants and the traders have come; their profits are pre-ordained..."[NEWLINE] - Sri Guru Granth Sahib[NEWLINE][TAB]

Gunpowder, also known as "black powder," was invented in China, possibly as far back as the 9th century AD, by alchemists looking for an elixir of immortality (which it isn't). A mixture of sulfur, charcoal, and potassium nitrate, gunpowder burns very rapidly when exposed to flame, producing a great quantity of gasses and solids which can be employed as a propellant in firearms and in fireworks. The Chinese used gunpowder in primitive bombs and rockets against the Mongol invaders, and once they conquered China, the Mongols used them against everybody else.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]By the first half of the 12th century AD the Arabic world acquired knowledge of gunpowder. Some historical texts state that the Mamluks used the first cannon in history against the Mongols during the Battle of Ain Jalut in 1260 AD, but this is open to debate. The first "hand cannon" appears in an Arabic manuscript from the 14th century.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Europe too gained knowledge of gunpowder towards the middle of the 12th century. They improved the quality of the powder by "corning" it, adding liquid to the powder to create larger grains (corns), increasing the explosive's stability.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Gunpowder remained the explosive of choice in cannon and firearms until the creation of "smokeless" powder in the 19th century. The new product burned cleaner and produced far less smoke, making it superior to the old black powder.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Musketman[ENDCOLOR], the first unit in the game which wields firearms.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The day when two army corps can annihilate each other in one second, all civilized nations, it is to be hoped, will recoil from war and discharge their troops."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Alfred Nobel[NEWLINE][TAB]

Technology is one of the driving forces behind civilization. It was advances in the technologies of agriculture and fishing that allowed cities to grow and thrive. It was advances in weaponry and masonry that allowed some cities to drive off the jealous barbarians who sought to steal their food and plunder their wealth. It was advances in medicine and sanitation that fought off the other great threat to civilization - disease.[NEWLINE]Advancing technology makes a civilization stronger, bigger, smarter and a much tougher opponent. It is critically important for a civilization to keep up technologically with its neighbors. Everything else being more or less equal, it is possible for a backwards civilization to overcome a more advanced neighbor, but it's pretty difficult to think of any examples of this occurring in history.

Trade involves the transfer of the ownership of goods or services from one person or entity to another in exchange for other goods or services or for money. Possible synonyms of "trade" include "commerce" and "financial transaction". Types of trade include barter. A network that allows trade is called a market. The original form of trade, barter, saw the direct exchange of goods and services for other goods and services. Later one side of the barter started to involve precious metals, which gained symbolic as well as practical importance. Modern traders generally negotiate through a medium of exchange, such as money. As a result, buying can be separated from selling, or earning. The invention of money (and later credit, paper money and non-physical money) greatly simplified and promoted trade. Trade between two traders is called bilateral trade, while trade between more than two traders is called multilateral trade.

Grants an additional [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] Trade Route. Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Caravan[ENDCOLOR], used to establish lucrative Trade Routes, and the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Market[ENDCOLOR], an excellent source of early [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"My kingdom for a horse!"[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Shakespeare (Richard III)[NEWLINE][TAB]

Renaissance Humanism was a cultural and educational reform originating in 14th and 15th Century Europe. Humanists sought to encourage the study of subjects that are now labeled as "humanities:" philosophy, history, language and religion. Foremost of the humanists was Desiderius Erasmus, whose Latin and Greek translations of the New Testament influenced the development of the Protestant Reformation.

Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Opera House[ENDCOLOR], which provides a large boost to [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. At least one civilization must have researched Humanism for the Protestant Reformation to commence.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Give light, and the darkness will disappear of itself."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Desiderius Erasmus [NEWLINE][TAB]
How can I speed up research speed?

Here are some common ways you can speed up your research (or your acquisition of technology): discover ancient ruins, enter into research agreements with other civilizations, construct buildings and wonders that improve your research output, earn a great scientist, and develop the rationalism branch in the social policy tree.

Industrialization is viewed as the transition from an agrarian society into an industrial one, which is typically accompanied by widespread social and economic change throughout the community. The Industrial Revolution, beginning in Europe during the 18th century, brought about immense changes in the way people lived their daily lives. With increasingly complex machinery and tools available, many trades that were once left to talented craftsmen became obsolete with the advent of assembly lines operated by droves of unskilled factory laborers.

Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Factory[ENDCOLOR], a building which greatly improves the [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production of a city. Also reveals [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aluminum, a resource used for many late-game units.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Industrialization based on machinery, already referred to as a characteristic of our age, is but one aspect of the revolution that is being wrought by technology."[NEWLINE] - Emily Greene Balch[NEWLINE][TAB]

The ancestry of the Internet lies in the development of ARPANET (Advanced Research Projects Agency Network), funded by the U.S. Department of Defense, for use by its university contractors and research labs in the exchange of information. It soon became a critical piece of the infrastructure for the scientific research community in the United States; tools and applications - such as simple mail transfer protocol (commonly referred to as e-mail) and file transfer protocol (FTP) for longer transmission - were developed in short order.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In the early 1980s, the Defense Department adopted the privately-developed transmission control protocol (TCP), which enabled different makes of computers on networks to route and reassemble data packets anywhere in the world. Along with the internet protocol (IP), a global address system, the TCP "open architecture" approach was enthusiastically accepted by most researchers and businesses around the world.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Within a few years, the network was transferring millions of bits per second, and several commercial networks were flourishing. In 1993 the University of Illinois made freely available "Mosaic," a new type of program for a new Internet technology dubbed the "World Wide Web." Within a few months, a number of corporations such as Netscape and Microsoft had entered the exploding field with browser and server software for use on personal computers. By the late 1990s there were approximately 100,000 Internet service providers around the world. In the first decades of the new century, the Internet was expanding an estimated 100% annually, making it the greatest conduit for information and entertainment in world history.
Increases [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism output of all cities by 50%, helping you advance toward a [ICON_VICTORY_CULTURE] [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Cultural Victory[ENDCOLOR].

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The Internet is the first thing that humanity has built that humanity doesn't understand, the largest experiment in anarchy that we have ever had."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Eric Schmidt[NEWLINE][TAB]

Iron working is older than history itself. The first iron worked probably came from meteorites; when this useful material was not to be found, the ancient people probably looked elsewhere for similar materials. Iron "smelting" - the extraction of the metal from iron ore - appears to have been discovered in the 12th century BC, in the Caucasus Mountains, Asia Minor, or possibly India. The production of wrought iron dates from approximately 1,000 BC.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The oldest examples of objects made from meteor iron are found in Ancient Egypt and Sumer and date back to 4,000 BC. Iron was extremely rare at that time, and historians speculate that it may have been more valued than gold.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]By the 12th century BC, iron largely replaced bronze as the metal preferred for tools and weapons in the Eastern Mediterranean. The iron of the time was not a better metal than the bronze it replaced, but it was far more abundant and could be found in many places where copper and tin weren't available, making it a whole lot cheaper.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The "modern" metal steel was first produced in prehistoric times, but the technology for large-scale production lagged far behind until the 17th century AD. Once steel became cheap and plentiful, it supplanted iron for most uses.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Swordsman[ENDCOLOR], an extremely powerful melee unit.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Do not wait to strike 'til the iron is hot; but make it hot by striking."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - William Butler Yeats[NEWLINE][TAB]

The term "laser" was originally spelled "LASER", as it is the acronym for "Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation", basically its own definition. The first scientific foundations for lasers were laid down by Albert Einstein in 1917 when he re-derived Planck's law of radiation, about the same time science fiction writers coincidentally began to describe a similar possible technology. The first functional laser wasn't demonstrated until 1960 when the Hughes Research Laboratories introduced laser technology capable of storing data via optical storage devices (like a DVD burner).[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Since this early laser research many different kinds of specialized lasers have been developed, ones which have been optimized for different functions like maximum firing range, output power, or utilizing different wavelength bands. While originally dubbed "a solution looking for a problem", lasers have found their way into thousands of different uses, from consumer electronics and entertainment to law enforcement and military use. Just try not to look directly into the light.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Nuclear Missile[ENDCOLOR], a frightening weapon that requires [ICON_RES_URANIUM] Uranium, and is capable of destroying units and cities.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - The Holy Bible: Romans, 13:12 [NEWLINE][TAB][TAB][TAB]

A machine is a device with moving parts (this is true during the pre-Electronics Age, anyway) that uses energy to perform tasks. A printing press is a machine, as is a loom, a clock and a watermill. Mastery of machinery requires design and engineering skill, of course, but also the ability to manufacture machine parts to precise measurements. A steam engine will leak if it's constructed poorly - that is, if it doesn't explode. The early Machine Age was a hugely dangerous time to work around the devices - if the fumes didn't kill you then you stood a fair chance of getting scalded, sucked into the works or blown to pieces.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]On the other hand, once a civilization began to master complex machinery, it gave them unrivaled wealth and power. England went early into the Industrial Revolution, and by so doing the small island nation dominated world trade for nearly three centuries.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Crossbowman[ENDCOLOR], a strong medieval ranged unit. Also increases the movement rate of units traveling along [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Roads[ENDCOLOR].
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The press is the best instrument for enlightening the mind of man, and improving him as a rational, moral and social being."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Thomas Jefferson[NEWLINE][TAB]

Masonry is the construction of structures from individual blocks bound together by some kind of mortar. The blocks may be made of stone, concrete, cinder, or they may be clay bricks. The mortar is some kind of workable paste that dries into an extremely durable material. It is usually composed of a mixture of sand, cement or lime, and water.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The ancient Egyptians mastered the art of masonry as early as the fourth millennium BC, constructing their temples, palaces and pyramids from the large veins of limestone, sandstone, granite and basalt found in the hills of the Nile River. The ancient Assyrians of the Fertile Crescent lacked such easy access to stone but possessed rich deposits of clay, which they sun-dried into bricks. Since sun-dried bricks can be vulnerable to moisture, they often covered their structures with more water-resistant kiln-baked or glazed tiles.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The ancient Romans invented concrete, which was a far superior mortar to that used by earlier civilizations (usually clay-based), and which could be used as a construction material in itself. This so-called "concrete revolution" allowed the Romans to construct buildings that were impossible using more primitive materials. In the 19th century a Parisian gardener thought to imbed iron mesh into his concrete tubs and pots; his invention of reinforced concrete greatly increased the "tensile strength" of the material, making it more suitable for tall structures that might be subject to stress from wind, vibration, or even earthquakes. More recent innovations have greatly increased the strength and flexibility of this most useful of all construction materials. And though many modern buildings are constructed of glass and steel, they all rest upon foundations built using the ancient construction techniques of masonry.

Allows you to build [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Walls[ENDCOLOR], which greatly improve the defense of cities from attack. Also allows Workers to construct [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Quarries[ENDCOLOR] on eligible resources.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"How happy are those whose walls already rise!"[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Virgil[NEWLINE][TAB]

The term "mass media" was coined in the 1920's with the advent of the radio, but the idea of media for large audience consumption has been around since the dramas and plays of the Ancient World. Mass media has been directly driven by technology, with greater advances in publishing techniques and communications leading to even larger possible audiences being reached.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Originally just applied to communication devices like radio, newspapers, and magazines, mass media now encompasses television, movies, music, paperback books, video games, and the Internet. With the advent of these globe-spanning media types has also arisen the ability to reach the masses like never before, and not always in a good way. The attempt to bias or control large amounts of information, either through nefariously minded propaganda or more innocent personal opinions being injected into facts, is becoming a large problem for some governments and organizations to deal with. Invasive advertising techniques are also a byproduct of mass media, much to the annoyance of consumers everywhere. While the message may be worthwhile and it's increasingly easier for the common person to publish their ideas and artworks, getting heard in the torrential output of information now available can really be like searching for that proverbial needle in the haystack.

Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Stadium[ENDCOLOR], which improves [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness in the empire, which in turn helps your city growth and makes [ICON_GOLDEN_AGE] Golden Ages more likely. Also allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Sydney Opera House[ENDCOLOR], a wonder very useful when pursuing a [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Cultural Victory[ENDCOLOR].

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The speed of communications is wondrous to behold. It is also true that speed can multiply the distribution of information that we know to be untrue."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Edward R. Murrow[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB][TAB]

Mathematics may be defined as the science of order, structure and relation that has evolved from counting, measuring and describing objects and their shapes. Mathematics is the most basic building block upon which all physical science is based. The Sumerians had a remarkably robust and complex mathematical system which was "base-ten" (like the modern system) and "base-60" as well. Remnants of the "base-60" system survive today primarily in modern time-keeping - 60 seconds to the minute, 60 minutes to the hour.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Egyptians had a somewhat simpler system, developed by the scribes/tax collectors, which was capable of performing the calculations needed to support huge engineering works like the pyramids (plus, one assumes, to keep track of uncollected taxes). The Greeks divided mathematics into two spheres, "arithmetic," the study of quantity, and "geometry," the study of magnitude, or area. Their primary contribution, however, lay in the application of theory and proof to mathematics. Previous mathematical systems were based upon measurement and observation of the real world, while the Greeks looked for the mathematical rules behind the reality.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Islamic world added much to mathematics in the 8th to 15th centuries AD. Perhaps most important was the invention of the decimal system for whole numbers, and the invention of the "0" (the number zero) some time around 600 AD in India. This replaced the extremely clunky and awkward "Roman" numerical system, which now survives only in horror movie sequel enumeration.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Mathematics has grown geometrically since its earliest beginnings, and through it man has split the atom, built the Internet, and constructed elaborate fantasy football leagues. Who knows what secrets it will unlock in the future?
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Skirmisher[ENDCOLOR], a mounted ranged unit specialized in harassment and flanking.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Mathematics is the gate and key to the sciences."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Roger Bacon[NEWLINE][TAB]

Metallurgy is the science of metals and metallic alloys. In Civilization V the "metallurgy" technology covers the advancements in this field since the 19th century AD. In the 19th and 20th centuries, great strides have been made in all facets of metallurgy, from extraction, to the creation of new alloys, to the production of cheap, high-quality metals.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Metal remains at the heart of modern civilization. Much of the world is built of steel, and what isn't is made of aluminum or titanium. Our communications networks are made of metal, and so are our vehicles, weapons, satellites and spacecraft. Without modern metallurgy 90% of the Earth's population would starve within a year.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Lancer[ENDCOLOR], a powerful Renaissance-Era mounted unit.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"There never was a good knife made of bad steel."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Benjamin Franklin[NEWLINE][TAB]

Metal casting is the process by which a craftsman can make one or more metal objects by pouring molten metal into a mold. One of the oldest methods of making a mold is the "lost wax" procedure, which dates back at least to the third millennium BC. In this process, the craftsman creates a wax duplicate of the object around which is built the mold; the wax is then melted and flows out of the mold and is replaced by molten metal. Once the metal cools the mold is opened and the object is removed.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Historically, sand and clay have been popular materials from which to construct molds. In later times molds have been constructed out of plastics and latex-like substances.
Allows you to build the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Baths[ENDCOLOR], which increase [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"When pieces of bronze or gold or iron break, the metal-smith welds them together again in the fire, and the bond is established."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Sri Guru Granth Sahib[NEWLINE][TAB]

Military Science is the science of using military power to achieve one's political goals. It has many branches and areas of expertise, and is generally taught in a military academy. For instance, how far can an army march in a day and how many calories does each soldier need to remain in top fighting condition? Or, how does one fight against an insurgency in our own country? Suppose we're an occupying army in another country; how does that change the approach to an insurgency?
